evidence.sourceQuote: Existing edited photos are preserved unless updateExisting=true

findings.message: The import contract says 'Existing edited records are preserved unless explicitly requested' (lightroom_catalog.rs:743) and 'Existing edited photos are preserved unless updateExisting=true' (library.importLightroom, cmd/library.rs:1391). In apply_prepared only develop settings are kept (keep_develop, 864-914); for every photo already in the library it unconditionally emits SetRating, SetFlag, SetLabel, SetMeta (keywords replaced wholesale at 891, XMP metadata merged at 875) and SetCaptured (915-922). Re-importing a catalog with updateExisting=false therefore silently overwrites ratings, picks, labels, keywords, metadata and capture-time corrections the user made in Ember, contrary to the documented default (recoverable only by undoing the whole import step).
findings.title: Either gate the rating/flag/label/meta/captured ops on update_existing (or on the photo being unedited) to match the contract, or narrow the doc comment, command help and docs/lightroom-catalog-import.md to say only develop edits are preserved.

changeAttribution.reason: Full-repo audit at a frozen HEAD; no baseline diff supplied.

evidence.sourceQuote: Move them to the new folder (copy and delete across drives).

findings.message: migrate(Move) deletes the source when a valid proxy already exists at the destination. The only same-folder guard is the lexical `new_dir == current` PathBuf comparison in smart_location (previews.rs). On macOS/Windows case-insensitive volumes, or via a symlink or a `..` spelling, the user can pick the same folder under another spelling (e.g. `/Users/a/Pictures/smart previews` for `/Users/a/Pictures/Smart Previews`). findings.title: Before removing src, skip when src and dst are the same file (compare canonicalized paths or (dev, inode)/file id), and have smart_location compare canonicalized directories rather than PathBuf equality.

evidence.action: Track interleaving with the monotonic s.commits() counter (record commits after each own step and flag interleaved when it differs on entry) plus an undo-pop counter, instead of undo.len().

changeAttribution.reason: Full-repo audit at a frozen HEAD; no baseline diff supplied.

evidence.sourceQuote: they are merged only while nothing else came in between (an Undo or an edit made meanwhile stays its own step, and the run's parts stay theirs).

findings.message: SyncCommit detects an Undo or edit made between its own steps only by comparing undo.len() with the length after its last step. Session::commit caps the undo stack at 1000 (lib.rs:516 removes the oldest entry), so once the history is full every commit leaves undo.len() unchanged; likewise an Undo followed by one edit restores the same length. In the app the SyncWork runs on a worker while the UI thread keeps accepting edits: with a full history, import batch committed -> user edits a photo -> Relink step committed, after_last == undo.len() so interleaved stays false, and finish() merges the last `own` (2) entries = [user edit, relink] into one 'Synchronize Folder' step. Undoing Synchronize Folder then also reverts the user's unrelated edit, contrary to the documented contract that an edit made meanwhile stays its own step.
findings.title: Track interleaving with the monotonic s.commits() counter (record commits after each own step and flag interleaved when it differs on entry) plus an undo-pop counter, instead of undo.len().

evidence.action: Download catalog entries from their exact url with lightcraft_fetch::download_url (which keeps the query and takes the local name from FileSpec), or reject at catalog parse time any url whose path does not end in `/<file_name>` with no query.

changeAttribution.reason: Full-repo audit at a frozen HEAD; no baseline diff supplied.

evidence.sourceQuote: each entry is a model manifest (the same fields as a `face-model.json`) plus the address to fetch it from

findings.message: Download.base() assumes the url ends in `/<file_name>`, an invariant enforced only by the built-in table's test (known.rs:199). User catalog entries break it: catalog::entry accepts any https url and derives file_name by stripping the query and filtering characters, and face_download passes spec.base() to lightcraft_fetch::download, which requests `<base>/<file_name>`. For the module's own documented shape `https://example.org/w/recogniser-r50.onnx?download=1` (catalog.rs test), strip_suffix fails, base() returns the whole url and the request becomes `.../recogniser-r50.onnx?download=1/recogniser-r50.onnx`. A url without an .onnx name (`https://host/files/123`) gets file_name `model.onnx` and fetches `https://host/files/123/model.onnx`. Signed or query-bearing catalog urls therefore cannot be downloaded, though the catalog accepts them.
findings.title: Download catalog entries from their exact url with lightcraft_fetch::download_url (which keeps the query and takes the local name from FileSpec), or reject at catalog parse time any url whose path does not end in `/<file_name>` with no query.

evidence.action: In BodyMode::Close over TLS, treat UnexpectedEof or a read_tls of 0 without close_notify as HttpError::Protocol (truncated), or require Content-Length or chunked for unpinned files; pinning sizes and hashes for vocab.json and merges.txt also closes it.

changeAttribution.reason: Full-repo audit at a frozen HEAD; no baseline diff supplied.

findings.message: For https, a TCP close without TLS close_notify (rustls UnexpectedEof), and a raw read_tls of 0, are both returned as a clean end of stream. Length and Chunked bodies catch this, but a response with neither Content-Length nor chunked encoding uses BodyMode::Close, where the 0 marks the body as Done. A network attacker who injects a FIN/RST can then truncate the body undetected. fetch_file keeps unpinned files (size None, sha256 None) once len > 0, and segment/src/fetch/mod.rs:20-21 downloads vocab.json and merges.txt exactly that way, so a truncated merges.txt is installed as complete and silently degrades the tokenizer.
findings.title: In BodyMode::Close over TLS, treat UnexpectedEof or a read_tls of 0 without close_notify as HttpError::Protocol (truncated), or require Content-Length or chunked for unpinned files; pinning sizes and hashes for vocab.json and merges.txt also closes it.

findings.title: Delete total_ram_gb and its or_else at line 90; let ci_jobs(None, cpus) use its existing default of 4 when available RAM is unknown (about 35 lines removed).

findings.message: When appimagetool is not on PATH the release packaging script downloads it from the moving `continuous` GitHub release with no version pin or checksum, executes it, and the AppImage it produces embeds that tool's runtime, which runs on every user's machine. A changed or compromised continuous build alters the shipped AppImage runtime without any change in this repository, and the cached copy in CARGO_TARGET_DIR is reused without re-verification.
findings.title: Download a pinned appimagetool release by tag and verify a recorded SHA-256 before chmod +x and execution (also when reusing the cached file).

evidence.action: Pin the package version in the URL and verify a recorded SHA-256 (or the package's NuGet signature) before extracting and loading the dlib.

findings.message: Azure Trusted Signing downloads whatever version of Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client nuget.org currently serves as latest, with no version pin, hash or signature check, then loads Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll into signtool while AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET and the other signing credentials are in the environment. A changed or compromised latest package executes arbitrary code with release-signing credentials, and an upstream breaking release silently changes the signing path of a release build.
findings.title: Pin the package version in the URL and verify a recorded SHA-256 (or the package's NuGet signature) before extracting and loading the dlib.

evidence.action: Reject rel values containing ':' or any non-Normal path component (use Path::components and require Component::Normal only), and canonicalize the result and require it to start with the canonical serve dir; optionally validate the Host header.

findings.message: The `cargo xtask web --serve` static server only rejects `..` components and backslashes. On Windows a request such as `GET /C:/Users/<u>/.ssh/id_rsa` yields rel `C:/Users/...`; Path::join with a path carrying a drive prefix replaces the base, so dir.join(rel) reads any file on disk and returns it with 200. The server binds 127.0.0.1 but performs no Host validation, so any local process, or a remote page via DNS rebinding, can read arbitrary developer files while the dev server runs.
findings.title: Reject rel values containing ':' or any non-Normal path component (use Path::components and require Component::Normal only), and canonicalize the result and require it to start with the canonical serve dir; optionally validate the Host header.

findings.message: Viewing a manual album sorted by capture date with the default filter re-sorts `visible` with `order.iter().position(..)` as the sort key. `position` is a linear scan of the album's photo list, and `sort_by_key` calls the key function O(n log n) times, so the sort costs O(n*m*log n). A 40k-photo album does on the order of 10^10 comparisons. `visible()` recomputes whenever the catalog revision changes, so every edit, rating or flag change in that album stalls the command or UI thread for seconds.
findings.title: Build a HashMap<PhotoId, usize> from `order` once and sort with `sort_by_cached_key`, or use `sort_by_key` over that map.

evidence.action: Build a HashSet of the existing/target ids once per command and use it for membership tests.

Each is O(album x targets). Importing into an album calls `album.addPhotos` once per batch of 8-16 photos against the growing album (`import_batch_done`). Adding 20k photos to a 20k-photo album, or a 40k-photo import into one album, costs hundreds of millions to billions of comparisons on the command thread. Each call also clones the full album Vec into `SetAlbumPhotos` and its undo inverse.
findings.title: Build a HashSet of the existing/target ids once per command and use it for membership tests.

evidence.action: Use visible_shared and compute the visible index range from the scroll viewport instead of walking all ids.

findings.message: filmstrip() copies the whole visible id list (visible_cloned = visible().to_vec()) and iterates every id each frame to compute a rect and an intersect test, though only about a dozen cells are on screen; the loupe prefetch at line 499 does a second full clone plus a linear position() scan per idle frame. The engine already offers visible_shared (Arc<[PhotoId]> with a generation). At 100k photos this is a per-frame O(N) allocation and walk.
findings.title: Use visible_shared and compute the visible index range from the scroll viewport instead of walking all ids.

evidence.action: When gain.channels == 1 compute one sample and one powf per pixel and reuse it for the three channels; hoist the per-row y coordinate; and parallelise apply() and compute() by rows with lightcraft_raster::par_rows as the neighbouring code does.

findings.message: gainmap::apply walks every pixel on one thread and, for each pixel, runs three bilinear gain.sample calls (four slice reads each) and three powf plus three exp2 even for the single-channel maps the encoder writes by default (channels==1 maps src=0 for all three channels, so the same sample and powf are computed three times). compute() likewise runs one log2 per pixel (three when multichannel) serially. On a 24 MP HDR gain-map export or decode this is on the order of seconds on one core while to_srgb8 and the JPEG encoder in the same pipeline use all cores, against the project's 1 s per 24 MP export budget.
findings.title: When gain.channels == 1 compute one sample and one powf per pixel and reuse it for the three channels; hoist the per-row y coordinate; and parallelise apply() and compute() by rows with lightcraft_raster::par_rows as the neighbouring code does.

evidence.action: Parallelise the per-pixel PQ/HLG conversion by rows (par_rows or rayon chunks, merging max/sum per chunk), use a lookup table for pq_encode, and pass the borrowed slice to write_image_data instead of copying it.

findings.message: encode_png_pq and the planes build in encode_avif_hdr convert pixels in a single-threaded loop that calls pq_encode (two powf) three times per pixel, plus a luminance accumulation and a growing Vec; for a 24 MP HDR export that is roughly 144 M powf calls on one core before the encoder starts. encode_png additionally copies the whole U8 sample buffer with to_vec() (up to ~100 MB for 24 MP RGBA) before handing it to the png writer.
findings.title: Parallelise the per-pixel PQ/HLG conversion by rows (par_rows or rayon chunks, merging max/sum per chunk), use a lookup table for pq_encode, and pass the borrowed slice to write_image_data instead of copying it.

evidence.action: Virtualize the candidate list (windowed rows with fixed height) and memoize the row component keyed by candidate and checked state; move form fields into a child component so typing does not re-render the list.

findings.message: ImportDialog keeps all review candidates (one per file in the chosen folder or card, unbounded) in component state and renders every one as a <label> with an ImportCandidatePreview in a plain map(). The same component owns the Keywords, Album, Destination, Rename and extension text fields, so each keystroke re-renders the entire candidate list, and each checkbox toggle copies the whole checked[] array and re-renders all rows. Importing a 5,000-photo card makes typing in any field and toggling selections visibly lag.
findings.title: Virtualize the candidate list (windowed rows with fixed height) and memoize the row component keyed by candidate and checked state; move form fields into a child component so typing does not re-render the list.

evidence.action: Key aggregate caches on a metadata/membership revision that develop-only ops do not bump, or skip invalidation for ops that touch only develop settings.

findings.message: Every Caches entry (counts, filter_values, date_groups, folder_tree, keyword_tree, people, album counts) is keyed on cat.revision, which Catalog::apply bumps for every op, including Op::SetDevelop applied during slider drags. Panels that are visible then recompute their O(N) library scans per drag step: counts walks all photos, filter_values clones and sorts every camera and lens string, date_groups and trees rebuild. Edits that cannot affect these aggregates still flush them, so editing a photo in a large library costs several full scans per frame.
findings.title: Key aggregate caches on a metadata/membership revision that develop-only ops do not bump, or skip invalidation for ops that touch only develop settings.

evidence.action: Stream: decode each sample, fold it into the look statistics (or a per-sample summary) and drop the buffer, decoding samples on a bounded worker pool; or lower the cap to what fits a fixed memory budget.

findings.message: look extract accepts up to 256 sample files and decodes every one to a linear Rgb32f (12 bytes per pixel, up to 1024x1024 = about 12.6 MB each) into the decoded Vec before extract_linear is called on the whole slice, so peak memory is up to about 3.2 GB (about 2 GB for typical 3:2 samples) and every decode is serial. On a modest machine 256 rendered samples exhaust memory or swap even though the statistics only need an accumulator per sample.
findings.title: Stream: decode each sample, fold it into the look statistics (or a per-sample summary) and drop the buffer, decoding samples on a bounded worker pool; or lower the cap to what fits a fixed memory budget.

evidence.action: Share column names (Arc<str> or index-based rows, or typed row structs) instead of cloning a String per cell, and extract only the needed columns while streaming rows into the per-photo structures.

findings.message: `Reader::table` reads every record of a table with `read_table` into memory and then converts each row to a `BTreeMap<String, Value>`. It clones every column name `String` for every row, on top of the whole database and WAL file bytes already held in RAM (up to 4 GiB). For a large Lightroom catalog, `Adobe_images` (about 40 columns) and the history-step and keyword tables, with hundreds of thousands of photos, create tens of millions of small String and BTreeMap node allocations. Resident memory is multiples of the catalog size and import start-up takes minutes. Tables over 1M rows are rejected, which for the optional history and keyword tables silently drops them with only a warning.
findings.title: Share column names (Arc<str> or index-based rows, or typed row structs) instead of cloning a String per cell, and extract only the needed columns while streaming rows into the per-photo structures.

evidence.action: Debounce the revision-triggered refresh (minimum interval regardless of revision, e.g. 5 s) or derive the count from session.media.availability instead of re-statting; avoid cloning all paths on the UI thread.

findings.message: missing_count treats the cache as stale whenever catalog.revision differs, and revision increments on every applied op, including Op::SetDevelop. While a slider is dragged (an op per change) each finished scan is immediately followed by another: the UI thread collects every library photo's path (missing::candidates) and a new worker thread stats every original file. On a 100k-photo library, or one on a network share, this is a continuous stat storm for the whole editing session, duplicating the cached Availability probe the app already has. The documented 'at most every 5 s' bound only applies when the revision is unchanged.
findings.title: Debounce the revision-triggered refresh (minimum interval regardless of revision, e.g. 5 s) or derive the count from session.media.availability instead of re-statting; avoid cloning all paths on the UI thread.

evidence.action: Route the count through Caches::rules_view (or key a cache on revision and rules) as the edit dialog does.

findings.message: The NewSmartAlbum dialog calls catalog.query(&rules, ...) (a full-library filter) and rebuilds filter_label on every frame the dialog is shown, uncached. The Edit smart album dialog uses Caches::rules_view keyed on revision and rules precisely to avoid this. With a large library every pointer move or keystroke while the dialog is open re-scans all photos, making the name field laggy.
findings.title: Route the count through Caches::rules_view (or key a cache on revision and rules) as the edit dialog does.

evidence.action: Do the serialisation snapshot on the UI thread but hand the bytes to a background writer thread (coalescing to the latest value), keeping sync_all there; keep the exit-time save synchronous.

findings.message: PrefsWriter::tick runs from eframe's logic() every frame and, every 3 s (or immediately when the library path changes), re-serialises the entire UiState with to_vec_pretty, compares it to the last write and, when anything changed, writes it on the UI thread with File::create, write_all, sync_all, rename and a directory sync_all. fsync on a busy disk, antivirus-scanned profile or network home regularly takes tens to hundreds of milliseconds, causing visible frame hitches whenever a panel is resized, a thumbnail slider is dragged or any persisted UI value changes.
findings.title: Do the serialisation snapshot on the UI thread but hand the bytes to a background writer thread (coalescing to the latest value), keeping sync_all there; keep the exit-time save synchronous.

evidence.action: Compute the count once per catalog revision and keyword (cache like Caches::keyword_ticks) instead of per frame.

findings.message: The RenameKeyword dialog scans every photo and every keyword (is_under) each frame just to show a count. Cost is O(photos x keywords) per frame while typing in the field on a large library.
findings.title: Compute the count once per catalog revision and keyword (cache like Caches::keyword_ticks) instead of per frame.

evidence.action: Compile a RuleSet once into a matcher (pre-lowered operand, parsed dates, a single now()/cutoff computed per evaluation pass) and evaluate that per photo; at minimum compute now()/shift_iso once per RuleSet::matches batch rather than once per photo.

findings.message: Rule::matches re-derives rule-constant data for every photo: lower(value) allocates (even for numeric fields such as rating, via other.to_string().to_lowercase()), date rules re-parse the rule date with rule_date for every photo, and inLast/notInLast call now() (thread-local clone or civil() format), then shift_iso which re-parses the current time and two fixed bound dates and formats twice, and the text rule builds a 14-field joined string plus keywords.join and people().join per photo. Smart albums and filters call this per photo over the whole catalog (Catalog::album_contains and query filtering), so a 100k-photo library with an 'in the last' smart album pays several allocations and four date parses per photo on every re-evaluation.
findings.title: Compile a RuleSet once into a matcher (pre-lowered operand, parsed dates, a single now()/cutoff computed per evaluation pass) and evaluate that per photo; at minimum compute now()/shift_iso once per RuleSet::matches batch rather than once per photo.

evidence.action: Refresh only after commands that mutate library/session state (or let the host return a revision in the command result and refresh only when it advanced), and do not await the refresh before resolving the command promise.

findings.message: Every non-UI command routed through run() (including read-only queries such as library.preferences, app.gpu, presets.list, photo.inspect and high-frequency edits) is followed by await refresh(), i.e. a full snapshot round trip through spawn_blocking and the session-owner channel before the caller's promise resolves. Opening Settings alone issues six queries, each chased by a snapshot; a burst of per-tick commands serialises on the snapshot latency instead of the command latency, working against the 16 ms slider budget.
findings.title: Refresh only after commands that mutate library/session state (or let the host return a revision in the command result and refresh only when it advanced), and do not await the refresh before resolving the command promise.

evidence.action: Skip setSnapshot when the new snapshot is structurally unchanged (compare a host-supplied revision/generation or a cheap hash), split rapidly changing status (jobs/progress) into its own context or selector so grid/inspector consumers do not subscribe to it, and drop JobDialog's separate interval in favour of the provider's single poll.

findings.message: DesktopProvider polls getSnapshot every 1200 ms (250 ms while importing/exporting/jobs) and calls setSnapshot(next) unconditionally. The IPC result is always a fresh object, so the single memoized context value (snapshot, ui, dialog, error, ...) changes on every poll and every useDesktop() consumer re-renders even when nothing changed. During a long import/export the cadence is 4 Hz, and JobDialog adds its own 300 ms setInterval that also calls refresh(), so the whole shell re-renders and the host session owner serves a full snapshot several times a second while the user is trying to keep working.
findings.title: Skip setSnapshot when the new snapshot is structurally unchanged (compare a host-supplied revision/generation or a cheap hash), split rapidly changing status (jobs/progress) into its own context or selector so grid/inspector consumers do not subscribe to it, and drop JobDialog's separate interval in favour of the provider's single poll.

evidence.action: Route the remaining pickers through the threaded PickRequest/picker path and run open_url/reveal on a background task (or spawn without waiting) like open_model_folder, delivering the result through the existing task callback.

findings.message: The comment at lines 450-451 records that a file dialog on the UI thread stopped the window answering the compositor, which then reported the app as hung (#191), and Services::picker moves its dialogs to a thread. The other services were not moved: pick_folder (used by Browse Folder, Move Folder To, Open Library, import dialogs), pick_files, pick_lightroom_catalog, pick_preset_files, save_preset_file and friends are called synchronously from the egui frame (left.rs:845 calls pick_folder inside the click handler), and open_url / reveal block on Command::status() for xdg-open (which can wait for a freshly launched browser or file manager) while the model-folder opener was already moved to a background task for that reason. Clicking Browse Folder freezes painting and input for as long as the dialog or launcher is open.
findings.title: Route the remaining pickers through the threaded PickRequest/picker path and run open_url/reveal on a background task (or spawn without waiting) like open_model_folder, delivering the result through the existing task callback.

evidence.action: Give DesktopHandle::snapshot a bounded recv_timeout and treat a timeout as 'busy' (prevent close and emit a notice); move shutdown_process off the event-loop thread (spawn it, then close the window from the completion) so the UI keeps painting.

findings.message: The CloseRequested branch of on_window_event runs on the main (event-loop) thread and calls host.snapshot(), whose call() waits on reply_rx.recv() with no timeout, and then host.shutdown_process(), which blocks for up to 30 s. If the session-owner thread is busy or wedged (a long synchronous command, a stalled volume, a deadlock), clicking the window close button freezes the entire UI, including the unsaved-changes and 'still running' prompts that depend on that snapshot, with no way to close short of killing the process; even a healthy slow shutdown freezes the window for up to 30 s with no feedback.
findings.title: Give DesktopHandle::snapshot a bounded recv_timeout and treat a timeout as 'busy' (prevent close and emit a notice); move shutdown_process off the event-loop thread (spawn it, then close the window from the completion) so the UI keeps painting.

evidence.action: Resolve on a helper thread and wait on a channel with the connect timeout, cancel and deadline checks, or document the exception.

findings.message: Stream::connect resolves the host with to_socket_addrs(), a blocking getaddrinfo call that honours neither the cancel flag, the connect timeout, nor the whole-operation deadline (limits.check() runs only before and after). With a broken resolver or captive network the worker thread blocks for the OS resolver timeout (often tens of seconds) after the user cancels a download or after the 20/45 s deadline of an OpenRouter request, contradicting the module's stated guarantee that a dead server or cancelled download never hangs the thread. Quit-time task waits are held up as well.
findings.title: Resolve on a helper thread and wait on a channel with the connect timeout, cancel and deadline checks, or document the exception.

evidence.action: Check metadata().len() (and that it is a regular file) first, or read through Read::take(MAX + 1) and fail if the limit is exceeded.

findings.message: migrate_preferences and persisted_library_path read the whole file with fs::read and only then compare the length to the 4 MiB cap, on the startup path in setup(). A pathological or corrupt legacy ui.json (multi-GB file, or a symlink to a device/FIFO such as /dev/zero) is fully loaded (or never returns) before being rejected, so a bad settings file can hang or OOM app launch instead of producing the intended 'exceeds N bytes' warning.
findings.title: Check metadata().len() (and that it is a regular file) first, or read through Read::take(MAX + 1) and fail if the limit is exceeded.

evidence.action: Continue the loop on EncoderStatus::Encoded, break only on LimitReached, and return Error::Encode when no KEY packet was produced (av1.is_empty()); add a round-trip test for encode_avif_hdr's success path.

findings.message: The rav1e receive loop treats EncoderStatus::Encoded as the terminal state (break) alongside LimitReached, but rav1e documents Encoded as 'a frame was encoded but no packet emitted yet, call receive_packet again' (ravif's own loop continues on it). If the first call after flush() returns Encoded, av1 stays empty, nothing checks av1.is_empty(), and avif_serialize::Aviffy::to_vec wraps zero bytes of image data in a valid-looking AVIF, so the HDR export reports success while writing an undecodable file (the originals may already be skipped or overwritten per the export conflict setting).
findings.title: Continue the loop on EncoderStatus::Encoded, break only on LimitReached, and return Error::Encode when no KEY packet was produced (av1.is_empty()); add a round-trip test for encode_avif_hdr's success path.

evidence.action: Wait for the short-lived launcher on a background thread (spawn a thread that calls child.wait() and logs a non-zero status) or use status() inside spawn_blocking.

findings.message: open_external spawns the opener (open -a, cmd start, xdg-open) and immediately drops the Child without wait(); Rust does not reap on drop, so on macOS every Edit in External Editor / Show in Folder leaves a defunct 'open' process until Ember exits, and the spawn error path logs nothing about the exit status, so an opener that fails after spawning (editor not found) is reported as success.
findings.title: Wait for the short-lived launcher on a background thread (spawn a thread that calls child.wait() and logs a non-zero status) or use status() inside spawn_blocking.

evidence.action: Make PngEncode return Result<Vec<u8>, String> and propagate the error through the control reply, or at minimum log the error and return an error reply when the encoded buffer is empty.

findings.message: The png service wraps encode_png(...).unwrap_or_default(); PngEncode returns Vec<u8>, so an encoding failure (zero or oversize dimensions, png writer error, out of memory) becomes an empty byte vector with no log and no telemetry. ui.screenshot / app.screenshot then pass those bytes to write() and reply ok:true with the path, leaving a zero-byte .png that scripts and CI treat as a successful screenshot (the CLI snapshot prints 'wrote ...' for it too).
findings.title: Make PngEncode return Result<Vec<u8>, String> and propagate the error through the control reply, or at minimum log the error and return an error reply when the encoded buffer is empty.

evidence.action: Add a timeout to the snapshot IPC (reject after a few seconds, clear refreshInFlight in finally as now, and surface the error), and make the host-side recv bounded; do not make command completion wait on the shared in-flight promise.

findings.message: refresh() deduplicates through refreshInFlight and returns the stored promise to every caller, and run() awaits refresh() after almost every command. getSnapshot() reaches host.snapshot(), which waits for the session owner with an unbounded recv(). If the owner is wedged (or the snapshot never replies), the in-flight promise never settles, refreshInFlight stays set forever, every later poll and every command awaiting refresh() hangs on the same pending promise, and no error is ever surfaced because neither .then nor .catch runs: the UI stops updating and every menu action appears to do nothing, with no recovery short of restarting.
findings.title: Add a timeout to the snapshot IPC (reject after a few seconds, clear refreshInFlight in finally as now, and surface the error), and make the host-side recv bounded; do not make command completion wait on the shared in-flight promise.

evidence.action: Log (and surface) the Err, and only mark the setting applied when execute succeeds.

findings.message: apply_settings records gpu_applied and memory_applied before executing app.gpu and app.memoryBudget and discards both results with let _ =. If the engine refuses the command (invalid budget, GPU init error) there is no log line, no toast and no retry, yet the Settings UI shows the value as active; a field report of 'memory budget ignored' leaves zero signal in the persisted log.
findings.title: Log (and surface) the Err, and only mark the setting applied when execute succeeds.

evidence.action: Share one launcher implementation with the egui app (rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler for URLs, raw_arg-quoted /select for reveal, ignore explorer's exit code on Windows).

findings.message: The desktop host's reveal() runs explorer with arg(format!("/select,{path}")) and requires a zero exit status. The egui app documents (issues #272 and #234, lightcraft/src/main.rs:395-413 and 385-388) that Rust quotes the whole switch when the path has a space so Explorer opens Documents instead of selecting the file, that the path must be backslashed and quoted via raw_arg, and that explorer exits non-zero even when it worked (hence its 's.success() || cfg!(windows)'). services.rs does none of this, so on Windows Show in Explorer opens the wrong folder for paths with spaces and returns 'reveal failed' when it did work; open_url likewise uses explorer, which the same file documents as opening File Explorer for URLs with a query or fragment.
findings.title: Share one launcher implementation with the egui app (rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler for URLs, raw_arg-quoted /select for reveal, ignore explorer's exit code on Windows).

evidence.action: Write each file into `.download` and `std::fs::rename` it into place, with the cities file last.

findings.message: The doc comment says the new place-name files replace the old ones only when complete, but `run` writes them with `std::fs::write` straight over the live files (states and countries first, then the cities file), not to staging followed by a rename. If the disk fills, the app is killed or a write fails part-way, the live `cities` file is left truncated (size and mtime changed) or the three files come from different downloads. `PlaceNames::load` then re-parses the truncated file and reverse geocoding silently fills wrong or missing places. A previously good dataset is destroyed by a failed refresh, and the user is told only that the download failed.
findings.title: Write each file into `.download` and `std::fs::rename` it into place, with the cities file last.

evidence.action: Wrap each `probe(..)` call in `crate::guard::catch` and map a panic to `Err(msg)` for that file, as `run_transfers` does.

findings.message: Import probes run untrusted camera/image files through `probe_bytes` (raw/EXIF/header parsing) on `thread::scope` workers with no per-file panic guard. The copy stage wraps each file in `guard::catch` (import.rs:1552) so one bad file becomes `PreparedItem::Failed`, but the probe stage has no such wrapper. A panic in the parser on one corrupt file kills that worker and `thread::scope` re-panics in the caller after the workers join. The whole scan or import of the folder fails, or on the app's scan worker thread the result is never delivered. The serial branch has the same gap. One damaged file among thousands blocks the import of all the others.
findings.title: Wrap each `probe(..)` call in `crate::guard::catch` and map a panic to `Err(msg)` for that file, as `run_transfers` does.

evidence.action: On an I/O failure of a pooled connection, retry once on a fresh connection before counting a failure, and make the failure count consecutive (reset on success) or time-decayed.

findings.message: `Remote` keeps pooled TCP connections open and the server closes idle connections after its 120 s timeout. `run_now` pops a pooled connection and, when the write or reply fails on a connection the server already closed, returns the error with no retry on a fresh connection. `try_run` adds it to `failures`, a cumulative counter that is never reset on success and has no time decay. After an idle gap or a brief network blip, up to `slots` (4) stale pooled connections each fail one tile. After `MAX_FAILURES` = 3 total failures `healthy()` stays false for the life of the loaded model. The remote GPU is permanently abandoned ("given up") for the session although the server is fine, and denoise silently runs on the local runner only.
findings.title: On an I/O failure of a pooled connection, retry once on a fresh connection before counting a failure, and make the failure count consecutive (reset on success) or time-decayed.

evidence.action: In the persisted-settings path, drop unknown/duplicate favourite ids (filter) instead of failing, or extend decode_saved_ui's field-level recovery to favoriteThemes as it does for docking; keep strict validation for control-channel writes if desired.

findings.message: favoriteThemes uses a deserializer that errors on any id not in ThemeKind::ALL. That error fails deserialization of the whole UiState in decode_saved_ui, which only has a compatibility recovery for `docking`; load_prefs_at then treats ui.json as damaged, renames it aside and starts with defaults, so library_path, recent libraries and the user keymap are lost for the session. A ui.json written by a build with an additional/renamed theme (downgrade, or a theme rename) triggers this from one favourite star. (Load path: apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs:226-277, decode_saved_ui / load_prefs_at.)
findings.title: In the persisted-settings path, drop unknown/duplicate favourite ids (filter) instead of failing, or extend decode_saved_ui's field-level recovery to favoriteThemes as it does for docking; keep strict validation for control-channel writes if desired.

evidence.action: Add `rename_all_fields = "camelCase"` to the enum (or `#[serde(rename = "maxDeviation", alias = "max_deviation")]` on the field) so that existing installed manifests still read.

findings.message: `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` on an enum renames only the variant names, not the fields inside struct variants. The JSON key is therefore `max_deviation`, while every other manifest key is camelCase, and the docs (line 34) and the validator error (`gain.maxDeviation`) say `maxDeviation`. A third-party denoise-model.json written as documented, `{"kind":"matchMean","nominal":1e6,"maxDeviation":0.05}`, fails manifest::parse with 'missing field max_deviation', so the model cannot be installed.
findings.title: Add `rename_all_fields = "camelCase"` to the enum (or `#[serde(rename = "maxDeviation", alias = "max_deviation")]` on the field) so that existing installed manifests still read.

evidence.action: Migrate legacy.language with normalizeLocale(legacy.language) when it maps to a supported LocaleCode, instead of a fixed list. Add a migration test for a pt-br legacy ui.json.

findings.message: The legacy egui UiState serializes `language` as a Locale code (en, zh-hans, zh-hant, ja, pt-br, es, de, ru, fr, uk). migrateLegacyUi only accepts the hard-coded subset ['en','zh-hans','zh-hant','ja']. A user who chose Portuguese (Brasil) in the egui app, which the React UI also supports (normalizeLocale maps pt-* to pt-br), loses that choice on migration and falls back to English. The migration contract drifted from the Rust Locale serialization it reads.
findings.title: Migrate legacy.language with normalizeLocale(legacy.language) when it maps to a supported LocaleCode, instead of a fixed list. Add a migration test for a pt-br legacy ui.json.

evidence.action: Use one shared tile limit: either cap manifest tiles at the remote/GPU limit (1024) or raise remote::MAX_TILE (and its payload bounds) to the manifest's 2048.

findings.message: Manifest validation accepts tiles up to 2048 cells, but the remote denoise protocol caps tiles at MAX_TILE = 1024, and serve() refuses to start beyond that. A valid model with tile 1536 installs and runs locally, but `lightcraft-cli denoise-serve` fails with 'tile size 1536 is outside 1..=1024', so its remote denoise can never be used. The two contracts disagree on the accepted range.
findings.title: Use one shared tile limit: either cap manifest tiles at the remote/GPU limit (1024) or raise remote::MAX_TILE (and its payload bounds) to the manifest's 2048.

evidence.action: Always store the final result in one shape (e.g. {report, indexWarning?, error?, path}, or always flatten the report and add indexWarning/error alongside) and document it in docs/control-protocol.md; add a test asserting the shape for both clean and index-warning completions.

findings.message: The final result of library.importLightroom (returned by wait:true and by status polling via lightroom_last) has two shapes for the same outcome: a clean import stores the engine report itself (top-level imported/failed/photos/... plus path), while an import whose archive index write failed or whose commit reported an error stores {report:{...}, indexWarning|error, path}. A control/MCP client reading result.imported gets the count on success but null when only the index write warned, although the photos were added; terminal() papers over this internally with value.get("report").unwrap_or(&value), but external consumers see the drift.
findings.title: Always store the final result in one shape (e.g. {report, indexWarning?, error?, path}, or always flatten the report and add indexWarning/error alongside) and document it in docs/control-protocol.md; add a test asserting the shape for both clean and index-warning completions.

evidence.action: Change the comment to reference VERSION ("version":V) as the module docs do.

findings.message: write_snapshot's contract comment says the catalog.snap bytes are exactly {"format":"lightcraft-catalog","version":1,...}, but the writer emits version {VERSION} (currently 8). Anyone building a reader or a fixture from this documented byte layout writes version 1, which Journal::open then treats as an older format and rewrites (reported as upgraded_from 1), and a v1-gated external tool would reject real snapshots.
findings.title: Change the comment to reference VERSION ("version":V) as the module docs do.

evidence.action: Keep the creator list structured (e.g. a Vec in Metadata), or split artist on the same "; " separator when writing so that read and write are inverses.

findings.message: dc:creator is an ordered rdf:Seq of creators. parse_xmp joins every entry into one string ("Alice; Bob") and write_xmp_lc writes Metadata.artist back as a single rdf:li. Because Ember's sidecar merge owns dc:creator (always replaced on save), a sidecar from another app with creators [Alice, Bob] is rewritten on Ember's next save as one creator "Alice; Bob", even when the user never edited the artist. Other readers then see one creator whose name contains a semicolon.
findings.title: Keep the creator list structured (e.g. a Vec in Metadata), or split artist on the same "; " separator when writing so that read and write are inverses.

evidence.action: Sum the widths with checked_add (as sraw.rs does) and reject any slice width greater than the frame's samples per row before slicing.

findings.message: The CR2 slice tag (CR2_SLICE) values s[1] and s[2] are taken from the file unbounded (only >0 checked) and summed with an unchecked iter().sum(). A crafted CR2 with, e.g., slices [1, 2^63, 2^63+1] makes the sum wrap to width=1 in release, which passes the total%width check. Mode::Full then executes data[y*width+x0 .. +sw] with sw=2^63 and panics (debug builds panic at the sum). Opening the file in the app crashes the decode thread, or aborts the web build (panic=abort). The sibling sRAW path uses try_fold/checked_add (cr2/sraw.rs:87).
findings.title: Sum the widths with checked_add (as sraw.rs does) and reject any slice width greater than the frame's samples per row before slicing.

evidence.action: Call decode_headers() first and reject a JPEG whose dimensions exceed the chunk's cw x ch (or MAX_SAMPLES), or set max_width/max_height to the chunk dimensions.

findings.message: For lossy DNG (compression 34892), decode_chunk bounds n=cw*ch*cpp by MAX_SAMPLES, but lossy_jpeg() hands the chunk to zune-jpeg with max width/height 65536 and never compares the JPEG's own frame header with the chunk dimensions before decode(). A tiny crafted DNG whose tile is a JPEG header declaring 65535x65535 RGB (with a truncated body, accepted because strict mode is off) makes the decoder allocate about 12.9 GB of output per tile. Tiles are decoded in parallel, so this exhausts memory or aborts on allocation failure. The only size check (line 239) runs after the allocation.
findings.title: Call decode_headers() first and reject a JPEG whose dimensions exceed the chunk's cw x ch (or MAX_SAMPLES), or set max_width/max_height to the chunk dimensions.

evidence.action: Do not route file opening through cmd.exe. Use ShellExecuteW through a maintained opener crate (e.g. the opener/open crate or tauri-plugin-opener), or call `explorer.exe <path>` / `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`, so no shell parsing happens. If cmd must stay, validate the path and pass it with raw_arg using cmd-safe quoting and caret-escaping. Add a regression test with a path that contains `&` and `%`.

findings.message: On Windows, with no external editor configured, open_external runs `cmd /C start "" <path>` and passes the photo path as an ordinary argument. Rust's Windows argument quoting only wraps arguments that contain a space or tab, and cmd.exe does not follow the MSVC escaping rules, so its metacharacters (&, |, ^, %VAR%) stay live. The path comes from the library: Edit in External Editor (photo.editInExternal -> photo.editExternal result path) sends it through lc_native openExternalEditor. Importing and then editing a photo named like `IMG&calc&.jpg` (no spaces) makes cmd run `calc` as a separate command. Any legitimate filename with an unspaced `&` also fails to open the right file.
findings.title: Do not route file opening through cmd.exe. Use ShellExecuteW through a maintained opener crate (e.g. the opener/open crate or tauri-plugin-opener), or call `explorer.exe <path>` / `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`, so no shell parsing happens. If cmd must stay, validate the path and pass it with raw_arg using cmd-safe quoting and caret-escaping. Add a regression test with a path that contains `&` and `%`.

evidence.action: Apply a short pre-authentication deadline (for example a 5 s read timeout until the first valid token line), and only then switch to the full timeout. Optionally cap connections per peer IP.

findings.message: The denoise server counts a connection against max_connections (default 8) when it is accepted, before any token check, and each connection may stay idle for the full 120 s read timeout. Any host that can reach the port, without knowing the token, can open 8 connections and send nothing, repeating every 2 minutes. Every legitimate client then gets 'server busy', so the remote GPU is denied to its owner. The listener is meant for a LAN/VPN, which limits who can reach it.
findings.title: Apply a short pre-authentication deadline (for example a 5 s read timeout until the first valid token line), and only then switch to the full timeout. Optionally cap connections per peer IP.

evidence.action: Route read_packet and sidecar_contents through the same bounded reader as import (read_sidecar_packet with MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES) and return an actionable error when the sidecar is larger.

changeAttribution.reason: whole-repo audit with no baseline commit (reviewContext.baseline not-applicable)

findings.message: Import caps a sidecar at MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES (4 MiB, import.rs:648-662), but read_packet (photo.readMetadataFromFile and other re-reads) reads any found .xmp whole with read_to_string, and for raws reads the entire original into memory; sidecar_contents (every save and XMP auto-write) likewise std::fs::read()s the existing sidecar unbounded. A hostile or corrupt multi-GB IMG_0001.xmp next to a photo makes the allocation fail, which aborts the process: a local file turns a metadata command into a crash, against the repo's own 'cap allocations sized by input' rule.
findings.title: Route read_packet and sidecar_contents through the same bounded reader as import (read_sidecar_packet with MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES) and return an actionable error when the sidecar is larger.

evidence.message: Result bound to `_`; the error is silently dropped

findingMessages.ai-slop-bt2020-pq-constants-repeated: The BT.2020 luminance weights `[0.2627, 0.6780, 0.0593]` are declared as three separate local consts (hlg_signal, encode_avif_hdr, encode_png_pq), and the ST 2084 constants M1/M2/C1/C2/C3 are declared twice (pq_encode, pq_decode). The sibling BT.601 weights are likewise a fourth local K. A later correction to one copy leaves the HDR AVIF, HLG and PQ PNG paths with different luma weights, producing silently inconsistent HDR output between formats.
findingMessages.ai-slop-cli-orphan-doc: The doc comment for library_error ("Why `--library DIR` can't be opened ... issue #99") was left stacked on top of library_warnings' own doc, so rustdoc/IDE hover shows a single merged comment on library_warnings and library_error (the function it describes) has no doc at all. Typical result of an edit that inserted a function between a comment and its item.
findingMessages.ai-slop-cli-test-comment-claims-undo: The comment says the apply step checks that "the values land, repeat-stable, undo restores", but the test never runs an undo or asserts restored values; it only compares two applyLook results (the second with dryRun=true) and a finite exposure. A regression in undo of develop.applyLook would pass this test while its comment claims coverage.
findingMessages.ai-slop-desktop-windows-open-diverges: The Tauri desktop host re-implements open_url/reveal for Windows without the fixes the egui app already carries for the same OS calls. services.rs open_url runs `explorer <url>`, which apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs documents (issue #234) as opening File Explorer instead of the browser for links with a query or fragment (e.g. an OpenStreetMap map link). services.rs reveal passes `format!("/select,{path}")` through Rust's arg quoting, which the same file documents (issue #272) as making Explorer open Documents instead of selecting the file whenever the path contains a space, and it does not strip the `\\?\` verbatim prefix. On Windows, Reveal in Explorer on `C:\My Photos\a.jpg` or opening a link with `?`/`#` from the desktop app misbehaves; the egui app has regression tests for exactly these cases, the desktop host has none.
findingMessages.ai-slop-help-urls-duplicate-links-table: HELP_URLS re-types the Help-menu link table that crates/ui-egui/src/links.rs already owns (LINKS/url_of), and the two have already diverged: app.help points to .../tree/main/docs here but to the repository root (HELP) in links.rs. The egui and desktop apps therefore send the same Help command to different pages, and any further URL change must be made twice.
findingMessages.ai-slop-path-validation-copy-paste: The same path guard `path.is_empty() || path.len() > 8_192 || path.contains('\0')` is pasted nine times across services.rs and native.rs with a bare 8_192 literal, while native.rs:770 already defines MAX_PERSISTED_LIBRARY_PATH = 8_192 that none of them use. Changing the limit or adding a rule (for example a newline or length-in-chars rule) means editing nine sites; sites missed will accept paths the others reject, and the error strings already differ ("invalid path", "invalid dropped path", "invalid library path").
findingMessages.ai-slop-sam3-size-literal-triplicated: The SAM 3 weights size 3439938512 is a magic literal twice in DialogHost.tsx (validation total and size label) and again as separate Rust constants in crates/segment/src/fetch/mod.rs:31 and crates/engine/src/segment/mod.rs:34. If the model file is replaced, the Rust side and the dialog's fallback progress/size disagree (percent computed against the stale total, wrong 'about N GB' text) unless all four are edited.
findingMessages.ai-slop-toneft-doc-links-test-only-fn: The ToneFit doc says `[fit_pairs_ordered]` tries the fits in order, but fit_pairs_ordered is #[cfg(test)]-only; the production path is search_ordered. In a non-test build the intra-doc link does not resolve and the comment points a reader at a function that does not exist in the shipped code.
findingMessages.ai-slop.duplicate-stacked-doc-raw-sample: `RAW_SAMPLES` has four stacked doc lines, the first two restating each other ('CC0 raw samples (raw.pixls.us). Small, representative set; extend freely (CC0 only).' / 'CC0 raw samples from raw.pixls.us (each verified CC0 on the site).'): two generations of the comment were appended instead of replaced, so the rustdoc is duplicated and the instruction pair reads as contradictory scope ('small set' vs 'one per format / compression variant').
findingMessages.ai-slop.orphaned-doc-comments-headless: In headless.rs `HeadlessView::painted_shapes` carries two stacked docs ('Every piece of text the last frame painted...' then 'Every shape of the last frame...'), so the first describes the wrong function and `painted_text` (line 191) has no doc. In the test module the doc 'The folder scan runs in the background: the request returns at once and the review opens when the scan finishes' is merged onto `browsing_the_same_folder_again_does_not_restart` (line 2962) while `add_folder_scans_in_the_background` (line 2994), the test it describes, has none; the first test's intent becomes unreadable.
findingMessages.ai-slop.orphaned-doc-comments-i18n: `builtin_label` (i18n.rs:215) is undocumented while its doc 'A stock preset's or profile's name in the UI language...' is stacked on top of `startup_failed_message`'s doc, so startup_failed_message's rustdoc opens with preset-name text. In tests, 'Locale tags are matched leniently, so a system locale reaches a shipped language.' is merged onto `startup_failure_message_names_the_error_and_the_log` instead of `locale_tags_normalize` (line 495).
findingMessages.ai-slop.orphaned-doc-comments-panels-and: Misattached docs: `fmt_gap` is documented 'Apply a dialog's action (also used by `ui.dialog.confirm`).' above its own '`90` -> `1 min 30 s`' line while `confirm_dialog` (dialogs.rs:1571), the function that sentence describes, has no doc; right.rs documents `copyright_status` with 'A labelled metadata text field: the typed text lives in egui memory...' while `meta_field` (right.rs:788) has none; menubar.rs `host_supports` ends with 'Restore and Delete Permanently replace Delete for photos in Recently Deleted', a sentence about a different item; corpus.rs documents `corpus_nef_high_efficiency_is_named` with the D7500 12/14-bit black-level paragraph, belonging to `corpus_nef_12_bit_black_level_matches_14_bit` (a test that has no doc). A reader of fmt_gap is told it applies dialog actions, and a failing corpus test points at the wrong stated intent.
findingMessages.ai-slop.orphaned-doc-comments-ui-lib: Doc comments in ui-egui/src/lib.rs are stacked on the wrong item, a copy-paste/merge tell. `slideshow_tick` carries 'Show a transient toast at the bottom of the canvas' while `pub fn toast` (line 720) has no doc; `HoverPreview` carries 'Whether the settings render in black & white' while `pub fn is_bw` (line 1389) is undocumented; the 'Every album's photo count for the sidebar... follow the clock within a minute' block sits above `rules_view` (merged with rules_view's own doc) while `album_counts` (line 1811) is undocumented. rustdoc then shows a wrong description for slideshow_tick, HoverPreview, rules_view and no description for toast, is_bw, album_counts.
findingMessages.ai-slop.test-only-helper-ignores-param: `loupe_request_dimensions` is `#[cfg(test)]`-only (no production caller) and accepts `_interactive: bool` that it never reads. Its test `interactive_loupe_request_keeps_full_display_dimensions` asserts `draft == full` between calls differing only in that ignored flag, which holds for any implementation, and the sizing it checks is a test-local reimplementation (`want = ...min(max_edge)`) rather than the production `AppSettings::loupe_edge` path, so the assertion cannot fail if the real loupe sizing regresses.
findingMessages.ai-slop.test-parses-serialized-json-text: `resetting_the_sidebar_brings_every_section_back` decides whether the Reset item is enabled by serializing the whole menu bar to a string, `find("view.sidebarReset")`, then splitting the rest of the text on `enabled":` and checking `starts_with("true")`. It reads whatever 'enabled' key follows the first textual hit, so a new field or reordered serialization (or the id appearing earlier in params/labels) makes it assert on another node's state; the typed `MenuNode::Item { enabled, .. }` walk is already used by `sidebar_menu_items` in the same file.
findingMessages.p0002-ai-slop-dead-param-pos: The closure `one` in parse_gps takes a `pos: char` hemisphere letter (callers pass 'N' and 'E') that is never read; `let _ = pos;` only silences the unused warning. The positive hemisphere letter is therefore not validated: a latitude typed as "51.5 E" or a longitude as "0.1 N" is accepted silently as positive instead of rejected.
findingMessages.p0002-ai-slop-misplaced-doc: The doc comment that describes merge_undo ("Fold the last `n` undo steps into one...") is stacked on top of the doc for commits(), so rustdoc renders one run-on doc on Session::commits() and Session::merge_undo, the function it describes, has no doc at all. A reader of the generated docs or an agent reading the signature is told commits() folds undo steps.

findingMessages.arch-dialoghost-shadowed-form-variants: EXPLICIT_FORM_KINDS and the FormDialog config define copysettings, pastesettings and cull forms, but DialogHost routes those kinds to GroupsDialog and CullReviewDialog before reaching FormDialog, so the FormDialog variants (including their payload shaping and the 'Choose groups in Inspector' note) can never render. Two implementations of the same dialogs exist, and a maintainer changing the FormDialog version sees no effect.
findingMessages.arch-duplicate-preferences-patch-paths-d: Preferences are patched through two IPC entry points with copy-pasted bodies that disagree when the desktop host failed to start: lc_preferences writes ui.json via preferences.patch and then returns Err(startup_error), while lc_native action preferences.patch performs the same write and returns Ok(value). The frontend therefore reports a failed save for a write that actually persisted (or a success, depending on which entry point the caller used), and fixes to one path do not reach the other.
findingMessages.arch-export-location-policy-two-authorit: removes_location() is the declared seam for location policy ('photo and catalog let library-level privacy rules add to the export option') and the Original/DNG path (prepare_guarded, export.rs:1753-1755) goes through it, but export_metadata() for every rendered format reads o.remove_location directly (export.rs:1597, 1610). The moment a library-level rule is added to removes_location as its doc invites, Original/DNG exports drop GPS while JPEG/TIFF/PSD/WebP/AVIF/JXL exports still embed GPS and place names, leaking the location the rule was meant to strip.
findingMessages.arch-qa-control-dispatch-parallel-comman: control_dispatch re-implements every tauri_commands handler (lc_run, lc_snapshot, lc_preferences, lc_native and its action chain) instead of sharing them, and the copies already diverge: QA lc_snapshot never applies mask_snapshot_gpu when gpu_recovery is set, QA lc_preferences/preferences.patch never clear gpu_recovery, never apply preference_patch_for_window and silently succeed with no host where lc_preferences returns the startup error, and QA saveBeforeClose ignores the caller-window ownership rule. native_qualification.rs drives only this copy (control.command("lc_snapshot"/"lc_preferences"/"lc_native")), so a GPU-crash-recovery or startup-failure regression in the production IPC handlers ships with a green native qualification run, and every new native action must be added in two dispatchers.
findingMessages.arch-qa-mode-detection-ungated-in-releas: QA mode is derived in five independent places with different gating. runtime_modes deliberately ignores LIGHTCRAFT_DESKTOP_QA/RIGHTKIT_QA_HIDDEN/RIGHTKIT_QA_BACKGROUND unless the qa-native feature is built (default = [] in Cargo.toml), but unattended_qa_enabled, build_shell, the lc_native import-picker guard and the macOS activation branch read the same variables unconditionally. A release build launched with any of those variables set (e.g. inherited from a developer or CI shell) therefore uses the production library and preferences while build_shell sets show_on_ready(false) and run() sets focus=false, so the main window never appears, and native pickers are rejected as 'unavailable in hidden QA'. This also leaves QA control behaviour compiled into release builds rather than stripped.
findingMessages.arch-session-catalog-public-bypasses-ops: lib.rs:7 documents the Catalog as 'mutated only by ops, so every change is undoable and journaled', but Session exposes it as a public mutable field. A frontend already bypasses it: desktop-host controller.rs:73 calls session.catalog.apply(Op::RemovePhoto) directly when --demo-count trims an opened library. That removal is not pushed to pending_log, not on the undo stack and skips apply_catalog's media.forget, so the in-memory catalog and the library's op log diverge (the photos come back on reopen, or a later snapshot/compaction persists the removal with no undo step).
findingMessages.arch-sync-pickers-bypass-parented-async-: services.rs documents that dialogs must be awaited from the caller's window on macOS instead of being dispatched synchronously from a worker, but the split is keyed on 'import' rather than on 'opens a dialog': pickPresetFiles, pickCurvePresetFiles, openFile, saveFile/saveExport/exportFile, savePresetFile, saveCurvePresetFile, pickTracklog, openLibrary, backupLibrary/restoreLibrary and selectFolder still run blocking rfd::FileDialog calls inside spawn_blocking with no parent window. These dialogs keep the unparented worker-thread behaviour the comment says to avoid (dialog not attached to the Ember window and able to open behind it), and the picker action list is maintained in four separate match tables.
findingMessages.p0002-arch-desktop-host-startup-policy-d: The two desktop hosts (egui `apps/lightcraft` and Tauri `apps/lightcraft-desktop`) each re-implement startup policy (CLI flags, library resolution order, GPU crash sentinel, crash notice text) instead of sharing one owner, and the copies have already diverged. In the egui host `--demo` is an alias of `--memory`, which its help text describes as a throwaway in-memory session where nothing is saved. In the Tauri host, `--demo` still resolves the user's real library (from the env var, the saved path or the default) and opens it on disk with seed_demo=true (controller.rs:58-61). A user or script that relies on the documented `--demo` throwaway mode ends up opening and writing their real library when they run the Tauri build. The GPU crash notice is also duplicated word for word (main.rs:175 and native.rs:950), so a wording or guidance fix has to be made in both places.
findingMessages.p0005-arch-faces-pump-twice-per-frame: logic_inner calls panels::faces::pump twice in the same frame (after slideshow_tick and again after model_setup::pump). The second call's faces.pump engine step is mostly suppressed by faces_next_pump, but watch_downloads is not gated: while a face-model download is watched, the engine command faces.models.downloads is executed twice per frame, and input-time bookkeeping runs twice. Duplicate orchestration of one subsystem in the per-frame loop.
findingMessages.p0005-arch-language-table-triplicated: A UI language is declared three times by hand: the language_table! entries (Locale::ALL order: ... Pt-BR, Es, De, Ru, Fr, Uk), LANGUAGE_COMMANDS (order: ... Pt-BR, Fr, Es, De, Ru, Uk) and language_from_command. The copies have already diverged in order: Settings > Language lists French after Russian (Locale::ALL), while Edit > Language lists it right after Portuguese (LANGUAGE_COMMANDS registry order). Adding a language means editing all three sites in step, and the coverage test only checks membership, not order.
findingMessages.p0005-arch-ui-command-dispatch-sprawl: UI commands are a string table (UI_COMMANDS, 158 ids) whose behaviour lives in a single ~1,525-line match in run_ui_command, with enabled state in a separate string match (ui_enabled) and checked/live-label state in menubar.rs. Nothing ties the table to the handlers at compile time: an id added to UI_COMMANDS but missed or misspelled in run_ui_command falls through `_ => return None` to the engine and fails as an unknown command at runtime, and menu enablement defaults to `true` for any id ui_enabled does not name. All 158 current ids are handled today (checked), so this is a change-risk/shotgun-surgery finding, not a live break.
findingMessages.p0006-arch-dialog-dispatch-scattered: Each Dialog variant is defined in state.rs (780-1018), but its behaviour is spread over separate exhaustive or partial matches in dialogs.rs: title (223-265), width (289-293), body (299-1120, inside the 1,143-line show() function), confirm_dialog (1571-1751), return_confirms (1946-1948), window_id (176-182) and keeps_open (1416-1418). Some dialogs delegate their body to their own module (Merge, Import, Settings, Sync, Denoise, Faces). Export instead renders 327 lines inline in one match arm (660-987). The partial matches (return_confirms, window_id, keeps_open, width) fall through silently, so a new dialog that needs Return-to-confirm, its own window id, or a stay-open rule compiles without them. The scattering already shows in the confirm_dialog doc comment, which has drifted onto fmt_gap (1400-1402).
findingMessages.p0006-arch-favorite-themes-strict-field-: favorite_themes uses a validating deserializer that returns an error for any unknown or duplicate theme id. An error in one field fails deserialization of the whole UiState. decode_saved_ui recovers only the docking field (main.rs:226-240), so load_prefs_at treats the whole ui.json as damaged: the file is renamed to ui.json.corrupt-* and every setting reverts to defaults, including library path, keymap, panel layout and appearance (main.rs:263-279). This happens when a ui.json written by a build with an extra or renamed theme id is opened by another build (downgrade, web vs native, or a theme removed later), or when the file is hand-edited. That is the opposite of the persistence policy the same file follows for the keymap, where a bad entry is ignored (shortcuts.rs:54-57).
findingMessages.p0006-arch-renaming-component-persisted: UiState mixes saved preferences with per-frame transient state, separated only by per-field #[serde(skip)]. renaming_component (an inline mask-component rename in progress) lacks the skip that its sibling renaming_mask (state.rs:621-622) has, so it is serialized. PrefsWriter::save_ui writes ui.json whenever the serialized state changes (main.rs:332-350), so starting a rename writes Some((mask_id, index, text)) to disk, and sanitized() (1209-1226) does not clear it. After a quit or crash mid-rename, the next launch restores it. masking.rs:309-315 then shows a rename field on any photo with a mask of that id and component index, and request_focus() on every frame takes keyboard focus away from other widgets until the user presses Esc or leaves the field. The stale text is also exposed through ui.get.
