findingMessages.correctness-cr3-framing-reference-fit-ro: estimate_cr3_framing fits the reference into the proxy's box with fit(), which keeps the reference's own aspect ratio, then returns None unless the size matches exactly. The comment on reference_at (398-402) records that this fit can round one pixel short (191x128 vs 192x128). When that happens, align_cr3_framing silently returns the unaligned sensor, so the CR3 framing correction is skipped for that file and the colour pairs are taken from misregistered pixels.
findingMessages.correctness-credits-undated-sort-descend: compare() orders undated (PR-only) contributors via dated()=(is_empty, date) so they sort after everyone with a date, as the comment at line 159 states. sorted() then applies o.reverse() for descending order, which also reverses that rule: with First/Last commit sorted descending (the ▼ toggle in the About window), every PR-only contributor with an empty date jumps to the top of the list ahead of the newest committers.
findingMessages.correctness-decision-manifest-source-fam: source_family_id is computed with virtual_identity(), which returns "original:<uuid>" for a master photo (masterImage 0) but "master:<master uuid>" for each of its virtual copies. A master and its virtual copies therefore get different source_family_id values. The manifest's own split_policy says any later split must keep source_family_id groups intact, so a consumer that groups by this field can put the master in train and a virtual copy of the same image in test, leaking the same source pixels across splits. The field is also a byte-for-byte duplicate of virtual_copy_identity, so it adds no family grouping at all.
findingMessages.correctness-dialog-confirm-errors-swallo: In dialogs::show, a confirm_dialog Err is only reported for Import/Export/ContactSheet/NewAlbum/NewSmartAlbum/SmartRules/KeywordTag/KeywordSet/SynchronizeFolder (toast) and SamModel; every other Err falls into `_ => close = true`, dropping the message. app.run does not toast errors itself. Example: Edit Capture Time with a typed time that is not a date makes photo.setCaptureTime return `... is not a date`, and the dialog simply closes with nothing changed and no message; likewise Rename Photos (on-disk rename failure), Merge (start_final 'a merge is already running' / plan error), Rename Keyword, Label Names, Paste Settings, Cull and Delete failures vanish silently and the user's input is lost.
findingMessages.correctness-hdr-maxfall-uses-luminance: MaxCLL is computed from the per-pixel max channel, but MaxFALL averages BT.2020 luminance. CTA-861.3 defines MaxFALL as the frame average of the per-pixel max(R,G,B); this is from the reviewer's recall and was not fetched. Saturated HDR content (a red highlight at 1000 nits has luminance of about 263) gets an understated MaxFALL in the PNG cLLI chunk and the AVIF content light level, which can make displays tone-map frames too brightly.
findingMessages.correctness-hover-preview-key-omits-phot: preview_job overwrites the key build_job made (which deliberately mixes in photo id and content: media.rs:1195-1197) with one from settings and size only. Two unedited photos from the same camera and aspect have identical develop settings, so hovering preset P on photo A and then stepping to photo B while still hovering P yields the same key. The UI's Renderer::request_needed (ui-egui render.rs:390-399) sees the Slot::Hover texture already holds that key and requests nothing, while the draw path filters that texture by photo (detail.rs:623): photo B never shows the hovered preset's look.
findingMessages.correctness-is-unedited-ignores-wb-edits: The doc says is_unedited ignores only white balance 'as shot' values, but the code overwrites the whole wb (mode, temp, tint) with the defaults. Photo::is_edited is `*develop != defaults && !develop.is_unedited()`. So a photo whose only edit is a white-balance change (for example mode Custom at 3200 K) counts as unedited. It is missing from edited filters and smart rules, and lens_ops/import treat it as untouched.
findingMessages.correctness-keywords-panel-overwrites-se: KeywordsPanel loads the keyword list of the active photo only (photo.inspect {id}), but add() and remove() send photo.setMeta {ids: snapshot.selection, keywords: next}. In the engine, `keywords` replaces the list (m.keywords.clear() then re-add) for every id. With photos A (active, keywords [beach]) and B (keywords [wedding, family]) selected, typing 'sunset' and pressing Add sets B's keywords to [beach, sunset]: B silently loses wedding/family and gains beach. Removing a chip likewise rewrites every selected photo to the active photo's remaining list.
findingMessages.correctness-library-switch-keeps-photo-i: Photo ids are per library (library.rs:420, 512), and the desktop app switches libraries on the same Session (ui-egui panels/settings.rs switch_library: close_library then open_library). open_stores resets undo/redo/selection/source but not Session::before (HashMap<PhotoId, settings>) nor Session::previous_active. After using Before/After 'Set Before' on photo 12 in library A and switching to library B, photo 12 of B renders A's settings as its Before side, and beforeAfter.copyBeforeToAfter/swap commits those foreign settings onto B's photo 12. Likewise develop.pastePrevious in B copies settings from whatever B photo has A's previous-active id.
findingMessages.correctness-lrcat-undo-merge-uses-capped: LRCAT import commits the file additions (import::commit_prepared, one undo step) and then the metadata/album batch (a second step), and merges them by comparing s.undo.len() with undo0 captured at lightroom_job.rs:304. Session::commit drops the oldest entry once the history exceeds 1000 (lib.rs:516-519), so in a session whose undo history is already full (1000 steps from ordinary slider edits) undo.len() stays 1000 after both commits: merge_undo(0) is a no-op. The import is left as two undo steps; one Undo removes the ratings/edits/albums but keeps the added photos, a partial undo of an operation that is supposed to be one step.
findingMessages.correctness-mcp-render-save-ignores-exte: render_photo always renders to a temporary .png and image_result re-encodes only when `format` is jpeg; it then writes those bytes to the caller's `path` without consulting the path's extension. An agent calling render_photo {path: "/tmp/look.jpg"} with no `format` gets PNG bytes saved under a .jpg name (screenshot behaves the same), while the headless app.export and ui.render paths pick the encoder from the extension.
findingMessages.correctness-merge-failed-options-survive: A merge preview fails for options X (spawn/plan error or the job returns Err) so app.merge.failed_options = Some(X). The user closes the dialog, selects a different set of photos and reopens the same merge kind: open() resets ids, error, preview and preview_pixels but never clears failed_options, and MergeDialog::for_command(command) yields the same default X. In poll(), stale = current != Some(opts) && !last_failed_matches(app, opts) is false because failed_options == X, so no preview is ever spawned for the new selection; with error cleared to None the preview box stays blank with no progress or message until the user changes an option.
findingMessages.correctness-p9-auto-import-ignores-sync-: Auto Import checks import/sync_run/lightroom only when it spawns the folder listing (lib.rs:1054-1058). The listing runs on a worker (it may take seconds on a network share); its done callback re-checks only app.import.is_none() before installing an ImportTask, and import::tick starts the worker without checking sync_run or lightroom. If the user confirms Synchronize Folder (sync.rs only refuses when app.import is Some) or starts an LRCAT import (lightroom busy() only refuses when app.import is Some) while the listing is in flight, the auto import then starts alongside it. That violates the module's stated invariant that an import and a Synchronize Folder never run at once because each readies files against the library as it was when it started, so both can add the same file (duplicate catalog records); likewise an auto import can run during a catalog import's commit window.
findingMessages.correctness-p9-rescan-drops-import-choic: Import from Device opens the review with Copy checked (menus.rs sets ScanTask.copy=true after import::open). If the user edits the scan filters and clicks Rescan, body() calls open_with_options, which always creates ScanTask{copy:false, album:None}; when that scan finishes, poll_scan replaces the whole dialog with ImportDialog::new(...) and sets d.copy=task.copy (false) and d.album=None. Move/destination/organize/rename/DNG/preset/keywords/new-album choices are also reset to defaults. A user who does not re-check the Transfer row then imports a memory card 'Add in place', so the library references files on removable media that go missing when the card is ejected; an album or keywords chosen before the rescan are silently not applied.
findingMessages.correctness-p9-review-start-replaces-run: import::start (the review dialog's OK / ui.dialog.confirm) checks only busy_synchronizing, unlike start_paths which refuses while app.import is Some or a review scan runs, and unlike lightroom busy(). With an Auto Import folder configured, an auto import (or a Local-view browse import) can start while the review dialog is open; confirming the dialog then assigns app.import = Some(new task), dropping the running ImportTask: its ImportRun Drop sets cancel, so remaining files are silently abandoned, any batches already sent but not yet committed are dropped without the Move rollback the worker performs on send failure, its committed batches are never merged into one undo step, and no completion/cancel toast is shown. Confirming during an LRCAT import likewise runs both at once although lightroom busy() treats an import as a conflict.
findingMessages.correctness-preview-failure-cached-forev: A render error is cached in `failed` under (slot, job key), and later requests with the same key are answered from the cache without rendering (render.rs:198). The only way to clear it for a live slot is Renderer::retry, and nothing in the repository calls it. A transient failure (a file briefly offline on an unmounted volume, or a memory-pressure decode error) therefore keeps replaying the same error for that photo and slot until the slot is evicted or the edit changes the key, even after the cause is gone.
findingMessages.correctness-reload-strips-duplicate-hash: photo.duplicate stores the copy's hash as '<hash>:dup<id>' (convert.rs:343), and other code strips that suffix before comparing (missing.rs stored_hash, sync.rs base_hash). content_op compares the fresh probe hash against the stored, suffixed hash directly. So Reload from Disk on an unchanged duplicate always reports it as changed: it adds an undo step, drops its cached sources, and writes SetContent with the bare hash. That removes the ':dup' marker the duplicate relied on to avoid clashing with its original's content hash.
findingMessages.correctness-remote-stale-pool-gives-up: Remote pools idle connections with no liveness check, while the server drops any connection idle past its 120 s read timeout (remote.rs:192). The engine keeps the loaded model, and so its Remote, for the next photo (denoise.rs `loaded`). If the user denoises a photo, waits more than 2 minutes, and starts another, every pooled connection is dead. Each try_run pops one, gets EOF ('the connection closed'), and counts a failure. With 4 slots, 3 failures reach MAX_FAILURES and the server is given up for the rest of the session: the remote GPU is never used again and the status shows 'given up', although the server is healthy.
findingMessages.correctness-remove-panel-size-control-un: The Remove panel's Size slider and number field only update local state `size`, which is never read or sent; spot.add takes its size from the drag distance in StageWorkspace (Math.max(0.005, |dx| || 0.025)). A user who sets Size to 0.2 and clicks the photo still gets a 0.025 spot, so the control does nothing.
findingMessages.correctness-segment-poll-drops-click-res: segment_poll treats 'pending counter is 0' as 'every reply has been sent', then clears segmenter.pending. The worker decrements the counter (drop(done)) before it sends the reply (worker.rs:277-278). If the UI frame polls in that window, idle is true, try_iter returns nothing, and pending is set to None; when the reply arrives next frame apply_outcome's Tag::Clicks branch sees pending != latest and returns, discarding the segmentation. The user's Object-mask click silently produces nothing and must be repeated.
findingMessages.correctness-shortcuts-cull-toast-ignores: The `cull` closure discards the result of app.run (line 400 only uses it for advance). The P/X/U and 0-5 key paths then toast 'Flagged as Pick' / 'Flagged as Reject' / 'Unflagged' / 'Rated ★★★' unconditionally (lines 435-440, 456-460). When the command fails (e.g. photo.pick's has_selection precondition with nothing selected, or a catalog write error), the user is told the photo was flagged/rated although nothing changed.
findingMessages.correctness-shortcuts-x-crop-double-rota: photo.reject and crop.rotateAspect are both engine commands declared with shortcut X, so in handle() one X press pushes both ids into `fire` (bindable loop, lines 360-370). With the Crop panel open, the photo.reject entry is redirected to crop.rotateAspect (line 509-511) and the crop.rotateAspect entry is NOT skipped (line 513 only skips it outside Crop), so it falls through to app.run at line 559. Pressing X once runs Rotate Crop twice: the aspect is swapped and swapped back (net no visible change) and two 'Rotate Crop' undo steps are recorded. The existing test library_keys_yield_to_search_and_crop_context only asserts the flag stays None, not that the crop rotated once. (Declarations: crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs:718 and crates/engine/src/cmd/develop.rs:784, both Some("X").)
findingMessages.correctness-xmp-iso-override: parse_xmp computes m.iso at line 511 with a >0 filter and an exifEX:PhotographicSensitivity fallback, then lines 512-514 unconditionally overwrite it with the unfiltered exif:ISOSpeedRatings value (parse_number already trims, so the override adds nothing but bypassing the filter). An XMP packet with exif:ISOSpeedRatings 0 (or a negative value) and a valid exifEX:PhotographicSensitivity of 6400 yields iso = Some(0) instead of 6400; a negative value saturates to Some(0) via `as u32`.
findingMessages.p0004-correctness-mask-id-truncation: Mask ids from command/MCP params are narrowed with `v as u32`, which wraps instead of rejecting. `mask.delete {id: 4294967297}` (2^32+1) resolves to mask id 1 and deletes (or renames/inverts/moves via the same mask_id helper) a different, existing mask than the caller named, instead of returning `no mask 4294967297`. mask.select (line 545) likewise selects an unrelated mask. This contradicts the repository rule that input-derived numbers are hostile and must use checked conversion.
findingMessages.p0004-correctness-placenames-nonatomic-r: The download's own contract (line 183) says the new place-name files replace the old ones only when complete, but each file is written in place with std::fs::write (truncate then write). If the disk fills or the app quits while writing the ~cities file (line 204), the previously working gazetteer is replaced by a truncated one. metadata.placeNamesStatus then reports `downloaded: true` (it only checks the file exists), and Fill Location from GPS silently finds fewer or no places. The optional files are also written (line 199) before the cities file, so a failure there leaves a mix of old and new data.
findingMessages.p0004-correctness-rename-start-overflow: photo.rename / photo.renamePreview take `start` as any u64 and cast it with `as usize`, with no upper bound. plan_rename_core iterates `(start..).zip(photos)`. With start = 18446744073709551615, RangeFrom::next overflows on the first step. In debug builds that panics: the command fails through the catch_unwind net rather than with a bad-params error. In release builds the sequence wraps to 0, 1, …. On 32-bit wasm, the `as usize` cast also silently truncates the value. This breaks the project's never-crash rule for hostile numeric input.
findingMessages.p0004-correctness-staging-filename-colli: Downloads::start only refuses a second download of the same model id; different models download side by side into one shared staging folder keyed only by spec.file_name. Catalog entries (catalog.json) derive file_name from the URL basename and fall back to `model.onnx`, so two catalog models can share a name and write the same `.downloads/<name>.part`. Concurrently, they corrupt each other's partial file and both fail. If one finishes and the second starts before the next faces.pump, the second fetch reuses or overwrites `<name>`. finish_downloads installs the first id with `verified: true` and its recorded sha (no rehash, face_models.rs:265). That can install the other model's bytes under the first model's manifest, or leave the first job's Done path pointing at a file that is gone.
findingMessages.p0006-correctness-geocode-high-latitude-: reverse() searches only the 3x3 block of 1-degree cells. One degree of longitude is 111 km x cos(lat), under MAX_KM (50 km) above about 63.3 degrees latitude, where cities15000 does list places (Tromso 69.6N, Murmansk 68.9N, Reykjavik 64.1N, Fairbanks 64.8N). A photo at 69.65N, 18.02E sits in cell 18; a place at 69.65N, 16.95E is about 41 km west, within MAX_KM, but lies in cell 16 (dx = -2) and is never examined, so the lookup returns a farther place in the 3x3 block or nothing.
findingMessages.p0006-correctness-smart-migrate-same-fol: migrate(Move) deletes the source when a valid proxy already exists at the destination. The only same-folder guard is the lexical `new_dir == current` PathBuf comparison in smart_location (previews.rs). On macOS/Windows case-insensitive volumes, or via a symlink or a `..` spelling, the user can pick the same folder under another spelling (e.g. `/Users/a/Pictures/smart previews` for `/Users/a/Pictures/Smart Previews`). Then for every proxy dst resolves to the same file as src, is_valid(&dst) is true and std::fs::remove_file(&src) deletes it: every smart preview is lost and counted as 'moved'. Smart previews are the only editable copy while originals are offline, so photos on an unplugged drive become uneditable.
findingMessages.p0006-correctness-sync-undo-interleave-a: SyncCommit detects an Undo or edit made between its own steps only by comparing undo.len() with the length after its last step. Session::commit caps the undo stack at 1000 (lib.rs:516 removes the oldest entry), so once the history is full every commit leaves undo.len() unchanged; likewise an Undo followed by one edit restores the same length. In the app the SyncWork runs on a worker while the UI thread keeps accepting edits: with a full history, import batch committed -> user edits a photo -> Relink step committed, after_last == undo.len() so interleaved stays false, and finish() merges the last `own` (2) entries = [user edit, relink] into one 'Synchronize Folder' step. Undoing Synchronize Folder then also reverts the user's unrelated edit, contrary to the documented contract that an edit made meanwhile stays its own step.
findingMessages.p0012-correctness-corpus-pngsuite-never-: `cargo xtask corpus` documents that --download fetches PngSuite and CC0 raw samples, and crates/codecs/tests/corpus.rs says corpus/pngsuite is fetched by that command, but cmd_corpus only iterates RAW_SAMPLES into corpus/raw. corpus/pngsuite is never created, so corpus_pngsuite (including the never-panic check on deliberately corrupt x* PNGs) silently skips on every machine and CI run that relies on the documented download, leaving PNG decoder corpus coverage permanently unexercised while appearing to pass.
findingMessages.p0012-correctness-static-check-substring: The desktop CI gate's 'static contracts' step reports bounded IPC/cache/stale-preview contracts as enforced by checking only that source files contain identifier substrings (sync_channel, MAX_JS_SAFE_ID, MAX_PENDING, DEFAULT_TTL, descriptor.sequence, MAX_SLICE = 512). A change that removes the bound enforcement while keeping the constant name or a comment mentioning it still prints 'desktop static contract: PASS (... IPC/cache contracts)', so the gate claims behavioural guarantees it never exercises (false coverage).

findingMessages.doc-cli-run-output-ms-on-failure: USAGE promises one JSON line per command shaped {"command", "ok", "result" | "error", "ms"}, but a failed step is emitted as {command, ok:false, error} with no ms field. findingMessages.doc-desktop-gpu-crash-notice-wrong-on-ma: After a GPU startup crash the user-facing notice says to re-enable 'Settings > Performance > Use the GPU for rendering' and to try LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND=dx12, vulkan or off. The Settings checkbox is actually labelled 'Use GPU rendering when available', and on macOS (a supported host for this binary) neither dx12 nor vulkan is a usable backend; metal, which parse_backends accepts (crates/gpu/src/backend.rs:11), is not mentioned. A macOS user following the recovery instructions sets a backend that cannot initialise.
findingMessages.doc-drift-p7-corpus-pngsuite-not-downloa: `cargo xtask` usage and crates/codecs/tests/corpus.rs both state that `cargo xtask corpus --download` fetches PngSuite into corpus/, but cmd_corpus only iterates RAW_SAMPLES into corpus/raw. corpus/pngsuite is never populated, so corpus_pngsuite always prints 'skip: ... absent' and returns; developers and CI believe PNG conformance coverage exists when it never runs.
findingMessages.doc-drift-p7-sony-corpus-count-stale: docs/sony-lens-corrections.md says the current `cargo xtask corpus --download` manifest holds 23 Sony samples across 17 bodies and that all of them are checked by sony_embedded_distortion_is_limited_to_validated_models. RAW_SAMPLES now also pins ILCE-7CM2 (2 files, issue #697) and ILCE-7RM6 ARW6 (2 files): 27 Sony files across 19 bodies. The 4 newer files are absent from the model-boundary test list, so the documented guarantee that every Sony corpus file is checked against the distortion model boundary is false for those bodies.
findingMessages.doc-drift-p7-tests-masking-module-doc-sc: The module doc says tests_masking.rs holds headless tests of the Masking and Remove tools, but it also holds smart-album editor, slideshow, Local folder tree, external-editor, soft-proofing and 100k-grid performance tests. findingMessages.doc-drift-p7-xtask-layering-doc-pointer-: xtask usage, the `layers` report header and the unregistered-crate violation message all direct the reader to plan/architecture.md §3, but plan/ is git-ignored and docs/architecture.md states that file is local-only. findingMessages.doc-drift.corpus-sraw-allowlisted-though: KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED still lists "sraw" as 'Canon sRAW / mRAW' not decoded, but cr2.rs now routes SRAW_TYPE=4 frames to vendor::cr2::sraw::decode, measured on the 31 CC0 sRAW/mRAW corpus samples. The corpus test accepts RawError::Unsupported for any file whose name contains 'sraw' (corpus.rs:87), so a regression that makes every sRAW/mRAW file Unsupported again passes the corpus gate silently instead of failing.
findingMessages.doc-drift.headless-painted-text-doc-misa: The doc line for painted_text ('Every piece of text the last frame painted...') sits above painted_shapes, so rustdoc shows painted_shapes as returning text in paint order and painted_text (line 191) has no doc at all; Headless::painted_text (line 295) links to HeadlessView::painted_text expecting that description.
findingMessages.doc-drift.raw-crate-doc-format-list-stal: The crate-level 'Formats' list omits containers decode() supports (Samsung SRW, Hasselblad 3FR/FFF via RawFormat::CfaTiff, Kodak DCS via RawFormat::KodakDcs) and its 'can't decode yet' list names only compressed ORF and CR3 variants, while corpus.rs:16 points to 'the crate docs' for a list that also includes Nikon HE NEF. RawFormat::OtherTiff's doc (line 115) still lists 3FR among undecoded TIFF raws although CfaTiff (line 109-112) says 3FR/FFF are read by the DNG reader. A maintainer or user reading the docs gets the wrong support matrix.
findingMessages.doc-export-module-not-pure: The module doc claims export is 'Pure (bytes in, bytes out) ... writing the file is the caller's job', but the module reads originals from disk (PreparedExport::run, export.rs:1817), owns the native file writer (write_file/write_file_durable, 1991-2008, creating folders and replacing files), and reserves/drives Apple Photos imports (after_export, 1954-1970). A caller relying on the documented purity (e.g. reusing it in the web build or a sandboxed context) gets filesystem and osascript side effects it was told it would not.
findingMessages.doc-lens-profiles-only-embedded-stale: crs.rs:396-398, files.rs:47-49 ('These are the only "profile" corrections Ember applies'), docs/xmp-interop.md:138 and docs/gaps.md:29 ('No lens profile database') all say profile corrections are only the file's own embedded ones. Since lens_profiles::for_raw (lens_profiles.rs:63-71) a lensfun-format database (LIGHTCRAFT_LENSFUN_DIR) also fills Photo.embedded_lens, which turns optics.lens_profile on by default (catalog model.rs:418-420). The XMP mapper's rule, built on the stale premise, ignores LensProfileEnable=0, so with a database configured a Lightroom sidecar/LRCAT edit that had profile corrections off imports with database distortion/vignetting correction on: the geometry and the imported crop no longer match the source edit.
findingMessages.doc-lrcat-existing-photos-preserved-over: The import contract says 'Existing edited records are preserved unless explicitly requested' (lightroom_catalog.rs:743) and 'Existing edited photos are preserved unless updateExisting=true' (library.importLightroom, cmd/library.rs:1391). In apply_prepared only develop settings are kept (keep_develop, 864-914); for every photo already in the library it unconditionally emits SetRating, SetFlag, SetLabel, SetMeta (keywords replaced wholesale at 891, XMP metadata merged at 875) and SetCaptured (915-922). Re-importing a catalog with updateExisting=false therefore silently overwrites ratings, picks, labels, keywords, metadata and capture-time corrections the user made in Ember, contrary to the documented default (recoverable only by undoing the whole import step).
findingMessages.doc-misplaced-item-docs: Doc comments sit on the wrong items, so rustdoc and IDE hovers describe the wrong API: Session::commits() (public) is documented as 'Fold the last n undo steps into one' while merge_undo(), which does that, has no doc (lib.rs:595-603); the description of the concurrent sidecar reader is attached to const MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES instead of read_sidecars (import.rs:645-648); 'Apply prepared normal-file results ... This function does no filesystem work' documents struct ApplyPrepared rather than fn apply_prepared (lightroom_catalog.rs:785-796).
findingMessages.p0002-doc-library-env-precedence: The module docs of the desktop app say the library comes from `--library`, else `$LIGHTCRAFT_LIBRARY`, else the last opened library. The resolver checks `EMBER_LIBRARY` first and falls back to `LIGHTCRAFT_LIBRARY` (library.rs:74-76). The inline comment at main.rs:824 leaves out the environment step entirely. findingMessages.p0002-doc-pastemetadata-fields-undocumen: The spec for photo.copyMetadata lists only title, caption, copyright, creator, location and keywords. An agent that follows the spec and passes fields:["location"] to paste a place gets only the sublocation string; City, State and Country are silently left alone. findingMessages.p0005-doc-locale-all-menu-order: Locale::ALL is documented as 'Every language, in menu order', but the Edit > Language menu is built from LANGUAGE_COMMANDS, whose order differs (French follows Portuguese there; in ALL it follows Russian). RAW_SAMPLES now also pins ILCE-7CM2 (2 files, issue #697) and ILCE-7RM6 ARW6 (2 files): 27 Sony files across 19 bodies. The 4 newer files are absent from the model-boundary test list, so the documented guarantee that every Sony corpus file is checked against the distortion model boundary is false for those bodies.

lensFindings.action: Point the xtask USAGE, cmd_layers header and layers.rs messages at docs/architecture.md#layers (the tracked document).

anchor.text: layers          enforce the crate dependency layering (plan/architecture.md §3)

lensFindings.failureScenario: xtask usage, the `layers` report header and the unregistered-crate violation message all direct the reader to plan/architecture.md §3, but plan/ is git-ignored and docs/architecture.md states that file is local-only. A contributor on a fresh clone who hits 'register it in xtask/src/layers.rs TABLE (see plan/architecture.md §3)' finds no such file; the tracked rules live in docs/architecture.md '## Layers'.

lensFindings.action: Add `version [set X.Y.Z[-pre]]` to the USAGE command list.
lensFindings.failureScenario: main dispatches `cargo xtask version [set X.Y.Z]` (the documented single source of truth for the workspace version used by packaging), but USAGE lists no `version` command, so `cargo xtask help` hides the version-bump entry point.

lensFindings.action: Move the unrelated tests into modules named for their features, or widen the module doc to describe what the file actually covers.
lensFindings.failureScenario: The module doc says tests_masking.rs holds headless tests of the Masking and Remove tools, but it also holds smart-album editor, slideshow, Local folder tree, external-editor, soft-proofing and 100k-grid performance tests. A developer changing those features searches the appropriately named modules, misses these regression tests, and the doc misdirects test ownership.

min-civil-delegate.action: Delete import::civil and call lightcraft_catalog::dates::civil at the three sites.

min-expand-within-duplicates-expand-with.action: Make one walker parameterised by (limits, filter) returning (files, truncated); express expand and expand_with_options through it.

min-import-defaults-free-fn-unused.action: Delete the free function; callers already use Photo::import_defaults().

min-interaction-original-dead.action: Delete the `original` field and its initialiser; keep `photo` and `originals`.

min-parse-gps-unused-param.action: Drop the `pos` parameter and the `let _ = pos;` line; call `one(&a, 'S')` and `one(&b, 'W')` with only the negative-hemisphere letter.

min-quick-image-srgb-duplicates-embedded.action: Extract `finish_preview_srgb(d, orientation_bytes, max_edge)` and call it from both.

min-read-sidecars-reimplements-workers.action: Replace the native branch with `let workers = workers(paths.len());` keeping the wasm `let workers = 1;` branch.

min-render-job-literal-repeated.action: Add a RenderJob constructor taking (photo, level, source, settings, request, key, cache, source_key) that fills the constant fields, and a helper for the variant cache/key pair.

min-render-result-literal-repeated.action: Build the result from self.failed(..) (or one RenderResult::new) and override only `rendered`/`loaded`/`gpu_fallback`/`display`; bind the failed-result base before self.info is moved.

min-source-total-duplicates-visible-filt.action: Extract `fn source_filter(&self, base: &Filter) -> Filter` doing to_filter plus the two source-specific fixups and call it from both.

minimize-detail-test-only-loupe-dimensio.action: Delete the helper and its call (keep the RenderJob draft/key assertions, computing dimensions inline or from the production path).

minimize-dialogs-export-repeated-rendere.action: Merge the adjacent `if rendered` blocks into one, and invert the empty-branch chain to `if rendered { if/else-if colour-space ladder }`.

minimize-dialogs-hand-rolled-key-of.action: Replace the 4-line hasher dance in both functions with `let key = crate::key_of((template, start, app.session.catalog.revision, &ids));` and `crate::key_of((id, app.session.catalog.revision, px))`; drop the `use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher}` lines.

minimize:state-sidebar-section-collapsed.action: Move it under #[cfg(test)] or have the tests call app.ui.sidebar.is_collapsed(SidebarSection::from_id(..)) directly.

minimize:tests-has-helper-copied.action: Hoist has/click/exec and the T/SETTLE constants into one shared #[cfg(test)] helper module (e.g. tests_support.rs) and import it.

p0001-01.action: Move the eval and corpus subcommands to a shared tools/research crate, or gate them behind a non-default feature, and keep run/mcp/render/snapshot/merge/commands in the shipped CLI.

p0001-02.action: Extract one synchronous dispatch function over (AppHandle, action, params, caller_label) and call it from both the Tauri command and the QA control plugin. That drops roughly 60 duplicated lines.

p0001-03.action: Add an AppState::host() -> Result<DesktopHandle, String> helper and route the preferences.patch action through the shared lc_preferences body.

p0001-04.action: Define one `fn valid_path_str(s: &str) -> bool` (or a `checked_path` returning Result) in services.rs and reuse it from services.rs and native.rs.

p0001-05.action: Collapse each picker pair to the async variant, or one shared builder, and drop the unreferenced aliases from run, is_import_picker and is_picker_action.

p0001-06.action: Delete the three diagnose_* probes and keep the existing failure-layout.json, failure-dom.json and failure-native.png capture.

p0001-07.action: Factor `parse_connect(args, &mut i)` and `open_headless(library, demo, imports)` helpers and call them from both subcommands.

p0001-08.action: Add `clampPreviewEdge`/`clampMemoryMb` helpers and a `runAndRefresh(id, params)` helper.

p0002-albumdialog-identical-ternary.action: Replace the ternary with the literal 'album.create'.

p0002-camera-preview-colour-closure-copi.action: Extract one `fn apply_colour(matrix: &Mat3, correction: Option<&HueSat>, x: [f64; 3]) -> [f64; 3]` (or a CameraLook method) and call it from all sites.

p0002-camera-preview-rank-correlation-du.action: Keep only rank_correlation_ties (renamed rank_correlation) and call it from fit_partial_on too; re-run the corpus look tests and bump LOOK_VERSION if any accepted look changes.

p0002-dialoghost-unreachable-form-kinds.action: Delete the 'cull', 'copysettings' and 'pastesettings' entries from EXPLICIT_FORM_KINDS and from FormDialog's config map, the matching payload branches in submit, and the two trailing Note/Check JSX fragments for those kinds.

p0002-library-source-and-removefolder-du.action: Extract `fn folder_ids(s, path, command) -> Result<Vec<PhotoId>>` for the shared checks and keep the per-command policy (disk flag) at each call site.

p0002-main-redundant-second-startup-mark.action: Delete the second `if !in_memory { begin_startup_marker(...) }` block in the creation closure.

p0002-rules-field-menu-triple-list.action: Add a group column (or Option<&str> group) to FIELDS and derive TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS/FIELD_GROUPS/field_group from it; the sync test then collapses to a uniqueness check.

p0002-settings-repeated-typeof-boolean-c.action: Add a small helper such as `pick = (key, check, fallback) => [supplied, persistedUi, persistedSettings].map(o => o[key]).find(check) ?? fallback` and call it per key; this removes roughly 10 long lines and the drift hazard.

p0004-corpus-skip-boilerplate.action: Add one helper such as fn corpus_file(dir: &Path, name: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> that reads the file, prints the skip line on NotFound and panics on other errors, and use it in every test; expected net cut of about 60-80 lines.

p0004-engine-tests-group-validation-dup.action: Drive the shared cases from one table: a helper taking (command, params-builder) that runs the invalid-name and invalid-type lists and asserts BadParams plus zero mutation, then keep only the command-specific happy-path assertions per test.

p0004-headless-tempdir-boilerplate.action: Provide one shared test helper (a test-support crate fn or the tempfile crate's TempDir with auto-cleanup) and replace the 30 inline sites and the per-module temp_dir copies.

p0007-total-ram-fallback.action: Delete total_ram_gb and its or_else at line 90; let ci_jobs(None, cpus) use its existing default of 4 when available RAM is unknown (about 35 lines removed).

findingMessages.min-civil-delegate: import::civil only forwards to lightcraft_catalog::dates::civil. view.rs:47 and cmd/manage.rs:139 already call the catalog function directly, so the engine carries a second public name for one function (callers: system_clock, files.rs:1059, tests).
findingMessages.min-expand-within-duplicates-expand-with: expand_with_options (432-462) and expand_within (465-494) are the same loop: skip check, is_dir -> walk::files_in, push explicit files, dedupe with a HashSet. They differ only in the file filter and the log message. expand_within's only callers are expand() and one test, so the production import path runs one copy while expand() (used by browse, missing, ui import) runs the other.
findingMessages.min-import-defaults-free-fn-unused: pub fn import_defaults(p) only returns p.import_defaults(). No caller of the free function exists in crates/, apps/ or xtask (every other hit is the Photo method or the Session field), so it is a dead public delegate.
findingMessages.min-interaction-original-dead: Interaction.original is set from begin_interaction (lib.rs:845) but never read: no `.original` access on an Interaction exists in crates/ or apps/. end_interaction/cancel_interaction and cmd/develop.rs use only `originals`, whose first entry is the same Arc. The doc comment ('Active-photo edits keep photo/original for existing callers') names callers that do not exist.
findingMessages.min-parse-gps-unused-param: The `one` closure in parse_gps takes `pos: char` that is never used (`let _ = pos;` at line 1635 silences the warning); both calls pass a hemisphere letter that does nothing.
findingMessages.min-quick-image-srgb-duplicates-embedded: embedded_preview_srgb (724-732) and quick_image_srgb (989-997) end with the same five steps: fit to max_edge with Filter::Box when larger, drop alpha, preview_orientation(...), to_srgb8().oriented(...). They differ only in where the decoded image comes from and which bytes give the orientation fallback.
findingMessages.min-read-sidecars-reimplements-workers: read_sidecars recomputes available_parallelism().clamp(1, MAX_IMPORT_PROBE_WORKERS).min(n) inline, which is exactly workers(jobs) defined at import.rs:1523 under the same cfg(not(wasm32)). A change to the worker policy (cap, fallback 4) has to be made in two places.
findingMessages.min-render-job-literal-repeated: Four builders (build_job, variant_job, face_job, Session::candidate_thumb_job) each write a 16-field RenderJob literal where request_id 0, stages/view_cache/display None, cache_generation and origin/info derivation are identical; variant_job and face_job also share the same cache+key tail (cache: Some((rendered, ck)), key: low^high of ck). Every new RenderJob field needs four edits.
findingMessages.min-render-result-literal-repeated: run_unguarded spells the same 11-field RenderResult literal three times (cache hit, closing-before-render, closing-after-render) although RenderJob::failed (867) already builds it. Adding a RenderResult field means editing every copy plus failed() and QuickJob's two copies (1079, 1096).
findingMessages.min-source-total-duplicates-visible-filt: source_total re-implements the Folder and LibraryFolder branches of visible() (browse path/subfolders, library_folder default '.') verbatim. A change to how a source maps to a filter (e.g. the '.' default) must be made twice or the grid count and total diverge.
findingMessages.minimize-detail-test-only-loupe-dimensio: loupe_request_dimensions is #[cfg(test)] only, has no production caller, and ignores its `_interactive` argument. Its only test calls it with true and false and asserts the results are equal, so the test proves a helper that mirrors nothing shipped and can drift from the real request-size code without failing.
findingMessages.minimize-dialogs-export-repeated-rendere: The Export dialog body tests `rendered` in three back-to-back `if rendered {` blocks (export_size, sharpen, metadata/watermark) with unindented bodies, and an `if !rendered {} else if ...` with an empty first branch. The repeated gate hides that these are one conditional section.
findingMessages.minimize-dialogs-hand-rolled-key-of: rename_preview and watermark_preview each hand-roll DefaultHasher::new()/hash/finish to build a cache key, although the crate already ships key_of(parts) (lib.rs:1580, same SipHash default, hash_one). Three copies of the idiom exist; a change to the key scheme must be made in each.
findingMessages.minimize:right-label-row-dead: pub fn label_row has no caller anywhere in crates/ or apps/ (repo-wide grep finds only its definition); it is dead code kept alive only by being pub in a pub(crate)-reachable module, so it carries a duplicate of the label/value painting logic for nothing.
findingMessages.minimize:state-sidebar-section-collapsed: UiState::sidebar_section_collapsed is pub in production code but its only callers are tests_panels.rs and other tests; no non-test code calls it (the sidebar uses self.sidebar.is_collapsed directly), so it is a test-only accessor shipped in release builds.
findingMessages.minimize:tests-has-helper-copied: The same 3-line `has(h, id)` widget-presence helper (and near-identical click/exec/T/SETTLE helpers) is redefined verbatim in 11 tests_*.rs modules (tests_panels, tests_album_picker, tests_activity, tests_date_picker, ...), so a change to how widgets are looked up must be repeated in every copy.
findingMessages.p0001-01: The shipped lightcraft-cli (packaged by release.yml and the FreeBSD package script) links about 5,500 lines of research harnesses (cull_eval 1550, personal_auto_eval 1525, decision_manifest/extract/plane, denoise_eval, measure_batch, cull_timing). Their own usage text calls them experimental and they take NEW_* private corpus paths. Every user build compiles and ships them, and their rayon/geom/color/raw deps exist only for them.
findingMessages.p0001-02: control_dispatch's lc_native arm re-implements the whole lc_native action ladder (openLibrary, backup/restore, preferences.patch, saveBeforeClose, window actions, model folders, import pickers) a second time for QA control. The two copies already differ (QA saveBeforeClose has no caller-label handling), so a fix to one silently misses the other.
findingMessages.p0001-03: Every Tauri command opens with the same host/startup_error clones and the same `host.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| error.unwrap_or_else(|| "desktop host is unavailable"...))` expression, repeated about 10 times in this file. The lc_preferences body and the `preferences.patch` branch of lc_native are near-identical copies, so a change to GPU-recovery handling must be made twice.
findingMessages.p0001-04: The path-sanity predicate `path.is_empty() || path.len() > 8_192 || path.contains('\0')` is pasted at 8 sites with 8 differing error strings, plus a MAX_PERSISTED_LIBRARY_PATH constant that duplicates the same 8_192. Changing the limit needs 9 edits.
findingMessages.p0001-05: services.rs keeps a sync picker path (pick_files, pick_files_with_params, run's dialog arms) and a duplicate async path (pick_files_async, pick_files_with_params_async, run_import_picker) with identical extension filtering and limit checks. Many action aliases (pickPhotos, importFolder, pickDevice, importDevice, importLightroom, saveExport, exportFile, import) have no caller in web/src, native.rs or the engine. Only the path-only contract test touches some of them.
findingMessages.p0001-06: diagnose_native_viewport_bounce, diagnose_stage_child_invalidation and diagnose_same_parent_layout (about 340 lines of ad-hoc DOM probe scripts) run only on macOS inside the failure path of with_control. They are leftovers from chasing one layout-bounce bug. They never assert anything and only write evidence on an already-failed run.
findingMessages.p0001-07: mcp() and run() each hand-parse `--connect [ADDR]` (identical port/addr heuristic), `--demo`, `--library`, and the same Headless-open sequence (open_library, library_error, library_warnings, import paths). snapshot() repeats the Session builder chain a third time. A fix such as the #1178 connect heuristic has to be applied to each copy.
findingMessages.p0001-08: The previewEdge clamp `Math.max(512, Math.min(16384, Math.round(x)))` and the memoryMb clamp `Math.max(0, Math.min(1_048_576, ...))` are each written out 3 to 4 times across migrateLegacyUi, clampUi and preferenceUi. In `run`, the `await runCommand(...); await refresh(); return value;` tail repeats about 12 times.
findingMessages.p0002-albumdialog-identical-ternary: AlbumDialog calls desktop.run(folder ? 'album.create' : 'album.create', ...): both branches are the same string, so the conditional is dead logic that suggests a distinct folder command that does not exist.
findingMessages.p0002-camera-preview-colour-closure-copi: The `matrix.apply(x)` followed by optional HueSat correction closure is copy-pasted in fit_pairs_on (852), fit_tone_only_on (1101) and fit_chroma (1307, with a slightly different borrow shape). fit_partial_on (998) uses a fourth, correction-less variant. A change to how a look's colour is applied must be made in each, and a missed copy silently fits tone against a different colour model than the one rendered.
findingMessages.p0002-camera-preview-rank-correlation-du: rank_correlation and rank_correlation_ties are two near-identical 20-line Spearman implementations; the second only adds tie handling (mean rank) and a symmetric variance guard. fit_partial_on still uses the weaker one while fit_tone_only_on and fit_tone_with_shadows use the tie-aware one, so quantized-luminance JPEGs are scored two different ways against the same PARTIAL_MIN_RANK_CORRELATION threshold.
findingMessages.p0002-dialoghost-unreachable-form-kinds: FormDialog carries config entries, payload branches and extra UI for 'cull', 'copysettings' and 'pastesettings' (and lists them in EXPLICIT_FORM_KINDS), but DialogHost routes those kinds earlier to CullReviewDialog (line 1009) and GroupsDialog (lines 1023-1024) before reaching the EXPLICIT_FORM_KINDS check at line 1029, so every one of those FormDialog branches is unreachable. A maintainer editing the cull or copy/paste form there changes nothing users see.
findingMessages.p0002-library-source-and-removefolder-du: library.source (libraryFolder arm) and library.removeFolder repeat the same sequence: reject blank/non-folder path via folder_key, reject is_startup_disk, build Filter{library_folder}, query, reject empty result with the identical message, then covers_other_disks. The two copies already differ in wording and in the disk:true escape hatch, so a fix to one rule (for example the startup-disk check) can miss the other.
findingMessages.p0002-main-redundant-second-startup-mark: begin_startup_marker is called before run_native (line 858) and again inside the eframe creation closure (line 933). MarkerTracker::begin_startup_marker only arms when startup_active is false, and nothing between the two calls clears startup_active (startup_succeeded runs on the first frame, after the closure), so the second call is a no-op that reads as if it re-armed the sentinel.
findingMessages.p0002-rules-field-menu-triple-list: The same 50 rule-field ids are written three times in the same order: FIELDS (with comment headers naming the groups), TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS and FIELD_GROUPS. A test (every_field_is_in_the_menu_exactly_once) exists only to keep the three lists in sync, which shows the duplication is a maintenance hazard: adding a field needs three coordinated edits or CI fails.
findingMessages.p0002-settings-repeated-typeof-boolean-c: SettingsDialog builds `initial` with a hand-repeated `typeof supplied.X === 'boolean' ? supplied.X : typeof persistedUi.X === 'boolean' ? ... : typeof persistedSettings.X === 'boolean' ? ... : desktop.ui.X` chain for confirmDelete, autoAdvance, filmstrip, filmNames, filmBadges, gridInfo, navigator, gpu (each about 250 characters, text/num variants likewise). Adding a setting means copying a 4-way chain again; one has already drifted (confirmDelete and gpu skip persistedSettings while the others consult it).
findingMessages.p0004-corpus-skip-boilerplate: crates/raw/tests/corpus.rs repeats the 'read corpus file, else eprintln skip: <name> absent and continue/return' block at 22 sites (two spellings: let-else Ok and a match on ErrorKind::NotFound), roughly 4-8 lines each. Each new corpus test copies it again, and the spellings already differ on whether a non-NotFound IO error panics (match form) or is silently skipped (let-else form).
findingMessages.p0004-engine-tests-group-validation-dup: develop_paste_validates..., develop_sync_validates..., develop_copy_and_paste_previous_validate_groups and presets_validate_groups_on_create_and_update re-state the same sequence (bogus group names, a 5-7 entry list of wrong-typed JSON, valid subset, omitted, explicit null) with only the command name changed; paste and sync are near line-for-line copies of about 70 lines each. A new group-taking command needs another 70-line copy.
findingMessages.p0004-headless-tempdir-boilerplate: headless.rs open-codes std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lc-...-{pid}")) + remove_dir_all + create_dir_all in 30 tests, and the same helper is separately redefined as fn temp_dir(tag) in about 19 other test modules (engine tests_*.rs, tests_preset_import.rs, tests_keyword_files.rs, preview/src/tests.rs, catalog/src/tests_lock.rs). Each also hand-rolls cleanup, so a failing assert leaks the directory and a stale pid-named dir can collide.
findingMessages.p0007-total-ram-fallback: total_ram_gb is a second per-OS probe (/proc/meminfo, powershell, sysctl) that only runs when available_ram_mb already failed, and halves installed RAM as a guess. On Linux and Windows the same file/PowerShell source that failed for available RAM is very likely to fail here too, so the fallback is largely dead flexibility; only a macOS vm_stat parse failure reaches it usefully.

findingMessages.perf-album-order-quadratic: Viewing a manual album sorted by capture date with the default filter re-sorts `visible` with `order.iter().position(..)` as the sort key. `position` is a linear scan of the album's photo list, and `sort_by_key` calls the key function O(n log n) times, so the sort costs O(n*m*log n). A 40k-photo album does on the order of 10^10 comparisons. `visible()` recomputes whenever the catalog revision changes, so every edit, rating or flag change in that album stalls the command or UI thread for seconds.
findingMessages.perf-album-vec-contains-quadratic: `album.addPhotos` tests `photos.contains(&t)` against the album's Vec for every target, `album.removePhotos` and `album.toggleTarget` test `targets.contains(..)` / `al.photos.contains(..)` per album photo, and select-by-criteria with `add` tests `ids.contains(&id)` per visible photo. Each is O(album x targets). Importing into an album calls `album.addPhotos` once per batch of 8-16 photos against the growing album (`import_batch_done`). Adding 20k photos to a 20k-photo album, or a 40k-photo import into one album, costs hundreds of millions to billions of comparisons on the command thread. Each call also clones the full album Vec into `SetAlbumPhotos` and its undo inverse.
findingMessages.perf-filmstrip-clones-and-walks-whole-vi: filmstrip() copies the whole visible id list (visible_cloned = visible().to_vec()) and iterates every id each frame to compute a rect and an intersect test, though only about a dozen cells are on screen; the loupe prefetch at line 499 does a second full clone plus a linear position() scan per idle frame. The engine already offers visible_shared (Arc<[PhotoId]> with a generation). At 100k photos this is a per-frame O(N) allocation and walk.
findingMessages.perf-gainmap-apply-serial-triple-work: gainmap::apply walks every pixel on one thread and, for each pixel, runs three bilinear gain.sample calls (four slice reads each) and three powf plus three exp2 even for the single-channel maps the encoder writes by default (channels==1 maps src=0 for all three channels, so the same sample and powf are computed three times). compute() likewise runs one log2 per pixel (three when multichannel) serially. On a 24 MP HDR gain-map export or decode this is on the order of seconds on one core while to_srgb8 and the JPEG encoder in the same pipeline use all cores, against the project's 1 s per 24 MP export budget.
findingMessages.perf-hdr-encode-serial-pq: encode_png_pq and the planes build in encode_avif_hdr convert pixels in a single-threaded loop that calls pq_encode (two powf) three times per pixel, plus a luminance accumulation and a growing Vec; for a 24 MP HDR export that is roughly 144 M powf calls on one core before the encoder starts. encode_png additionally copies the whole U8 sample buffer with to_vec() (up to ~100 MB for 24 MP RGBA) before handing it to the png writer.
findingMessages.perf-import-candidates-unvirtualized: ImportDialog keeps all review candidates (one per file in the chosen folder or card, unbounded) in component state and renders every one as a <label> with an ImportCandidatePreview in a plain map(). The same component owns the Keywords, Album, Destination, Rename and extension text fields, so each keystroke re-renders the entire candidate list, and each checkbox toggle copies the whole checked[] array and re-renders all rows. Importing a 5,000-photo card makes typing in any field and toggling selections visibly lag.
findingMessages.perf-library-caches-flushed-by-every-dev: Every Caches entry (counts, filter_values, date_groups, folder_tree, keyword_tree, people, album counts) is keyed on cat.revision, which Catalog::apply bumps for every op, including Op::SetDevelop applied during slider drags. Panels that are visible then recompute their O(N) library scans per drag step: counts walks all photos, filter_values clones and sorts every camera and lens string, date_groups and trees rebuild. Edits that cannot affect these aggregates still flush them, so editing a photo in a large library costs several full scans per frame.
findingMessages.perf-look-extract-retains-all-decoded-sa: look extract accepts up to 256 sample files and decodes every one to a linear Rgb32f (12 bytes per pixel, up to 1024x1024 = about 12.6 MB each) into the decoded Vec before extract_linear is called on the whole slice, so peak memory is up to about 3.2 GB (about 2 GB for typical 3:2 samples) and every decode is serial. On a modest machine 256 rendered samples exhaust memory or swap even though the statistics only need an accumulator per sample.
findingMessages.perf-lrcat-row-materialization: `Reader::table` reads every record of a table with `read_table` into memory and then converts each row to a `BTreeMap<String, Value>`. It clones every column name `String` for every row, on top of the whole database and WAL file bytes already held in RAM (up to 4 GiB). For a large Lightroom catalog, `Adobe_images` (about 40 columns) and the history-step and keyword tables, with hundreds of thousands of photos, create tens of millions of small String and BTreeMap node allocations. Resident memory is multiples of the catalog size and import start-up takes minutes. Tables over 1M rows are rejected, which for the optional history and keyword tables silently drops them with only a warning.
findingMessages.perf-missing-count-restat-on-every-revis: missing_count treats the cache as stale whenever catalog.revision differs, and revision increments on every applied op, including Op::SetDevelop. While a slider is dragged (an op per change) each finished scan is immediately followed by another: the UI thread collects every library photo's path (missing::candidates) and a new worker thread stats every original file. On a 100k-photo library, or one on a network share, this is a continuous stat storm for the whole editing session, duplicating the cached Availability probe the app already has. The documented 'at most every 5 s' bound only applies when the revision is unchanged.
findingMessages.perf-new-smart-album-dialog-queries-ever: The NewSmartAlbum dialog calls catalog.query(&rules, ...) (a full-library filter) and rebuilds filter_label on every frame the dialog is shown, uncached. The Edit smart album dialog uses Caches::rules_view keyed on revision and rules precisely to avoid this. With a large library every pointer move or keystroke while the dialog is open re-scans all photos, making the name field laggy.
findingMessages.perf-prefs-writer-fsync-on-ui-thread: PrefsWriter::tick runs from eframe's logic() every frame and, every 3 s (or immediately when the library path changes), re-serialises the entire UiState with to_vec_pretty, compares it to the last write and, when anything changed, writes it on the UI thread with File::create, write_all, sync_all, rename and a directory sync_all. fsync on a busy disk, antivirus-scanned profile or network home regularly takes tens to hundreds of milliseconds, causing visible frame hitches whenever a panel is resized, a thumbnail slider is dragged or any persisted UI value changes.
findingMessages.perf-rename-keyword-dialog-scans-library: The RenameKeyword dialog scans every photo and every keyword (is_under) each frame just to show a count. Cost is O(photos x keywords) per frame while typing in the field on a large library.
findingMessages.perf-rule-matcher-per-photo-invariants: Rule::matches re-derives rule-constant data for every photo: lower(value) allocates (even for numeric fields such as rating, via other.to_string().to_lowercase()), date rules re-parse the rule date with rule_date for every photo, and inLast/notInLast call now() (thread-local clone or civil() format), then shift_iso which re-parses the current time and two fixed bound dates and formats twice, and the text rule builds a 14-field joined string plus keywords.join and people().join per photo. Smart albums and filters call this per photo over the whole catalog (Catalog::album_contains and query filtering), so a 100k-photo library with an 'in the last' smart album pays several allocations and four date parses per photo on every re-evaluation.
findingMessages.perf-run-awaits-full-snapshot: Every non-UI command routed through run() (including read-only queries such as library.preferences, app.gpu, presets.list, photo.inspect and high-frequency edits) is followed by await refresh(), i.e. a full snapshot round trip through spawn_blocking and the session-owner channel before the caller's promise resolves. Opening Settings alone issues six queries, each chased by a snapshot; a burst of per-tick commands serialises on the snapshot latency instead of the command latency, working against the 16 ms slider budget.
findingMessages.perf-snapshot-poll-context-churn: DesktopProvider polls getSnapshot every 1200 ms (250 ms while importing/exporting/jobs) and calls setSnapshot(next) unconditionally. The IPC result is always a fresh object, so the single memoized context value (snapshot, ui, dialog, error, ...) changes on every poll and every useDesktop() consumer re-renders even when nothing changed. During a long import/export the cadence is 4 Hz, and JobDialog adds its own 300 ms setInterval that also calls refresh(), so the whole shell re-renders and the host session owner serves a full snapshot several times a second while the user is trying to keep working.
findingMessages.perf-ui-thread-blocking-host-services: The comment at lines 450-451 records that a file dialog on the UI thread stopped the window answering the compositor, which then reported the app as hung (#191), and Services::picker moves its dialogs to a thread. The other services were not moved: pick_folder (used by Browse Folder, Move Folder To, Open Library, import dialogs), pick_files, pick_lightroom_catalog, pick_preset_files, save_preset_file and friends are called synchronously from the egui frame (left.rs:845 calls pick_folder inside the click handler), and open_url / reveal block on Command::status() for xdg-open (which can wait for a freshly launched browser or file manager) while the model-folder opener was already moved to a background task for that reason. Clicking Browse Folder freezes painting and input for as long as the dialog or launcher is open.

findingMessages.p0004-resilience-1: `cargo xtask corpus --download` runs curl with no --connect-timeout/--max-time/--retry, writing straight into the final path. A stalled connection hangs the command indefinitely; a mid-transfer failure leaves a truncated file at `out`. The `?` aborts the whole run, and the next run sees `out.exists()`, skips the download, fails the sha256 check, deletes the file and errors again; only the third run actually re-downloads. One transient network error therefore costs two failed runs, and one bad sample stops every later sample from being fetched.
findingMessages.p0004-resilience-2: The script creates a keychain at a fixed path ($TMP/lightcraft-signing.keychain-db), prepends it to the user's keychain search list, and its EXIT trap removes only the .p12. If the script is run again on a machine whose TMP persists (a self-hosted runner or a local run), `security create-keychain` fails because the file exists and `set -e` aborts the signing job. Any failure after line 36 also leaves the temporary keychain on the search list.
findingMessages.res-close-handler-blocks-main-thread: The CloseRequested branch of on_window_event runs on the main (event-loop) thread and calls host.snapshot(), whose call() waits on reply_rx.recv() with no timeout, and then host.shutdown_process(), which blocks for up to 30 s. If the session-owner thread is busy or wedged (a long synchronous command, a stalled volume, a deadlock), clicking the window close button freezes the entire UI, including the unsaved-changes and 'still running' prompts that depend on that snapshot, with no way to close short of killing the process; even a healthy slow shutdown freezes the window for up to 30 s with no feedback.
findingMessages.res-dns-resolve-ignores-cancel-and-deadl: Stream::connect resolves the host with to_socket_addrs(), a blocking getaddrinfo call that honours neither the cancel flag, the connect timeout, nor the whole-operation deadline (limits.check() runs only before and after). With a broken resolver or captive network the worker thread blocks for the OS resolver timeout (often tens of seconds) after the user cancels a download or after the 20/45 s deadline of an OpenRouter request, contradicting the module's stated guarantee that a dead server or cancelled download never hangs the thread. Quit-time task waits are held up as well.
findingMessages.res-fs-read-before-size-cap: migrate_preferences and persisted_library_path read the whole file with fs::read and only then compare the length to the 4 MiB cap, on the startup path in setup(). A pathological or corrupt legacy ui.json (multi-GB file, or a symlink to a device/FIFO such as /dev/zero) is fully loaded (or never returns) before being rejected, so a bad settings file can hang or OOM app launch instead of producing the intended 'exceeds N bytes' warning.
findingMessages.res-hdr-avif-packet-loop-accepts-empty: The rav1e receive loop treats EncoderStatus::Encoded as the terminal state (break) alongside LimitReached, but rav1e documents Encoded as 'a frame was encoded but no packet emitted yet, call receive_packet again' (ravif's own loop continues on it). If the first call after flush() returns Encoded, av1 stays empty, nothing checks av1.is_empty(), and avif_serialize::Aviffy::to_vec wraps zero bytes of image data in a valid-looking AVIF, so the HDR export reports success while writing an undecodable file (the originals may already be skipped or overwritten per the export conflict setting).
findingMessages.res-open-external-child-never-reaped: open_external spawns the opener (open -a, cmd start, xdg-open) and immediately drops the Child without wait(); Rust does not reap on drop, so on macOS every Edit in External Editor / Show in Folder leaves a defunct 'open' process until Ember exits, and the spawn error path logs nothing about the exit status, so an opener that fails after spawning (editor not found) is reported as success.
findingMessages.res-png-encode-error-swallowed: The png service wraps encode_png(...).unwrap_or_default(); PngEncode returns Vec<u8>, so an encoding failure (zero or oversize dimensions, png writer error, out of memory) becomes an empty byte vector with no log and no telemetry. ui.screenshot / app.screenshot then pass those bytes to write() and reply ok:true with the path, leaving a zero-byte .png that scripts and CI treat as a successful screenshot (the CLI snapshot prints 'wrote ...' for it too).
findingMessages.res-refresh-inflight-never-settles: refresh() deduplicates through refreshInFlight and returns the stored promise to every caller, and run() awaits refresh() after almost every command. getSnapshot() reaches host.snapshot(), which waits for the session owner with an unbounded recv(). If the owner is wedged (or the snapshot never replies), the in-flight promise never settles, refreshInFlight stays set forever, every later poll and every command awaiting refresh() hangs on the same pending promise, and no error is ever surfaced because neither .then nor .catch runs: the UI stops updating and every menu action appears to do nothing, with no recovery short of restarting.
findingMessages.res-startup-settings-failures-swallowed-: apply_settings records gpu_applied and memory_applied before executing app.gpu and app.memoryBudget and discards both results with let _ =. If the engine refuses the command (invalid budget, GPU init error) there is no log line, no toast and no retry, yet the Settings UI shows the value as active; a field report of 'memory budget ignored' leaves zero signal in the persisted log.
findingMessages.res-windows-launchers-regress-known-issu: The desktop host's reveal() runs explorer with arg(format!("/select,{path}")) and requires a zero exit status. The egui app documents (issues #272 and #234, lightcraft/src/main.rs:395-413 and 385-388) that Rust quotes the whole switch when the path has a space so Explorer opens Documents instead of selecting the file, that the path must be backslashed and quoted via raw_arg, and that explorer exits non-zero even when it worked (hence its 's.success() || cfg!(windows)'). services.rs does none of this, so on Windows Show in Explorer opens the wrong folder for paths with spaces and returns 'reveal failed' when it did work; open_url likewise uses explorer, which the same file documents as opening File Explorer for URLs with a query or fragment.
findingMessages.resil-geocode-nonatomic-dataset-write: The doc comment says the new place-name files replace the old ones only when complete, but `run` writes them with `std::fs::write` straight over the live files (states and countries first, then the cities file), not to staging followed by a rename. If the disk fills, the app is killed or a write fails part-way, the live `cities` file is left truncated (size and mtime changed) or the three files come from different downloads. `PlaceNames::load` then re-parses the truncated file and reverse geocoding silently fills wrong or missing places. A previously good dataset is destroyed by a failed refresh, and the user is told only that the download failed.
findingMessages.resil-import-probe-panic-aborts-scan: Import probes run untrusted camera/image files through `probe_bytes` (raw/EXIF/header parsing) on `thread::scope` workers with no per-file panic guard. The copy stage wraps each file in `guard::catch` (import.rs:1552) so one bad file becomes `PreparedItem::Failed`, but the probe stage has no such wrapper. A panic in the parser on one corrupt file kills that worker and `thread::scope` re-panics in the caller after the workers join. The whole scan or import of the folder fails, or on the app's scan worker thread the result is never delivered. The serial branch has the same gap. One damaged file among thousands blocks the import of all the others.
findingMessages.resil-remote-denoise-permanent-giveup: `Remote` keeps pooled TCP connections open and the server closes idle connections after its 120 s timeout. `run_now` pops a pooled connection and, when the write or reply fails on a connection the server already closed, returns the error with no retry on a fresh connection. `try_run` adds it to `failures`, a cumulative counter that is never reset on success and has no time decay. After an idle gap or a brief network blip, up to `slots` (4) stale pooled connections each fail one tile. After `MAX_FAILURES` = 3 total failures `healthy()` stays false for the life of the loaded model. The remote GPU is permanently abandoned ("given up") for the session although the server is fine, and denoise silently runs on the local runner only.

findingMessages.p0004-schema-placenames-undocumented-bas: metadata.downloadPlaceNames reads a `base` parameter (the download address, line 221) and rejects non-https values with "`base` must be an https:// address". Its published contract (line 286) declares only `{dataset?: folder}` and states the data comes from download.geonames.org. Schema-driven callers cannot know the parameter exists, and the contract's claim about the source is not enforced by the implementation.
findingMessages.p0004-schema-renamepreview-contract-clai: The published command contract for `photo.renamePreview`, a non-journaled `query` that only returns plan_rename's plans, is copied verbatim from photo.rename. It says the command renames the files on disk (sidecars too) and is undoable. An MCP agent or UI that chooses commands from this schema text may treat the preview as the mutation: it reports files as renamed when nothing changed, or avoids calling the preview because it believes the preview is destructive.
findingMessages.p0006-schema-catalog-download-url-filena: Download.base() assumes the url ends in `/<file_name>`, an invariant enforced only by the built-in table's test (known.rs:199). User catalog entries break it: catalog::entry accepts any https url and derives file_name by stripping the query and filtering characters, and face_download passes spec.base() to lightcraft_fetch::download, which requests `<base>/<file_name>`. For the module's own documented shape `https://example.org/w/recogniser-r50.onnx?download=1` (catalog.rs test), strip_suffix fails, base() returns the whole url and the request becomes `.../recogniser-r50.onnx?download=1/recogniser-r50.onnx`. A url without an .onnx name (`https://host/files/123`) gets file_name `model.onnx` and fetches `https://host/files/123/model.onnx`. Signed or query-bearing catalog urls therefore cannot be downloaded, though the catalog accepts them.
findingMessages.schema-favorite-themes-strict-voids-ui-j: favoriteThemes uses a deserializer that errors on any id not in ThemeKind::ALL. That error fails deserialization of the whole UiState in decode_saved_ui, which only has a compatibility recovery for `docking`; load_prefs_at then treats ui.json as damaged, renames it aside and starts with defaults, so library_path, recent libraries and the user keymap are lost for the session. A ui.json written by a build with an additional/renamed theme (downgrade, or a theme rename) triggers this from one favourite star. (Load path: apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs:226-277, decode_saved_ui / load_prefs_at.)
findingMessages.schema-gain-max-deviation-key-not-camelc: `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` on an enum renames only the variant names, not the fields inside struct variants. The JSON key is therefore `max_deviation`, while every other manifest key is camelCase, and the docs (line 34) and the validator error (`gain.maxDeviation`) say `maxDeviation`. A third-party denoise-model.json written as documented, `{"kind":"matchMean","nominal":1e6,"maxDeviation":0.05}`, fails manifest::parse with 'missing field max_deviation', so the model cannot be installed.
findingMessages.schema-legacy-ui-language-drops-supporte: The legacy egui UiState serializes `language` as a Locale code (en, zh-hans, zh-hant, ja, pt-br, es, de, ru, fr, uk). migrateLegacyUi only accepts the hard-coded subset ['en','zh-hans','zh-hant','ja']. A user who chose Portuguese (Brasil) in the egui app, which the React UI also supports (normalizeLocale maps pt-* to pt-br), loses that choice on migration and falls back to English. The migration contract drifted from the Rust Locale serialization it reads.
findingMessages.schema-manifest-tile-exceeds-remote-limi: Manifest validation accepts tiles up to 2048 cells, but the remote denoise protocol caps tiles at MAX_TILE = 1024, and serve() refuses to start beyond that. A valid model with tile 1536 installs and runs locally, but `lightcraft-cli denoise-serve` fails with 'tile size 1536 is outside 1..=1024', so its remote denoise can never be used. The two contracts disagree on the accepted range.
findingMessages.schema-p9-lightroom-result-shape-drift: The final result of library.importLightroom (returned by wait:true and by status polling via lightroom_last) has two shapes for the same outcome: a clean import stores the engine report itself (top-level imported/failed/photos/... plus path), while an import whose archive index write failed or whose commit reported an error stores {report:{...}, indexWarning|error, path}. A control/MCP client reading result.imported gets the count on success but null when only the index write warned, although the photos were added; terminal() papers over this internally with value.get("report").unwrap_or(&value), but external consumers see the drift.
findingMessages.schema-snapshot-doc-version-drift: write_snapshot's contract comment says the catalog.snap bytes are exactly {"format":"lightcraft-catalog","version":1,...}, but the writer emits version {VERSION} (currently 8). Anyone building a reader or a fixture from this documented byte layout writes version 1, which Journal::open then treats as an older format and rewrites (reported as upgraded_from 1), and a v1-gated external tool would reject real snapshots.
findingMessages.schema-xmp-dc-creator-seq-collapsed: dc:creator is an ordered rdf:Seq of creators. parse_xmp joins every entry into one string ("Alice; Bob") and write_xmp_lc writes Metadata.artist back as a single rdf:li. Because Ember's sidecar merge owns dc:creator (always replaced on save), a sidecar from another app with creators [Alice, Bob] is rewritten on Ember's next save as one creator "Alice; Bob", even when the user never edited the artist. Other readers then see one creator whose name contains a semicolon.
