p0004-security-download-pinning-invarian.action: Correct the invariant to say catalog.json entries are user-supplied addresses verified by their declared hash/size (or restrict them to https).

p0004-security-keyword-export-overwrites.action: Call `s.check_write_target(path)` before writing (as export.contactSheet does) and write atomically.

p0004-security-placenames-unpinned-base.action: Drop the `base` parameter from release builds (keep it behind cfg(test)/debug for the loopback test server) or pin the GeoNames files by size/hash.

p0006-security-tls-truncation-accepted-a.action: In BodyMode::Close over TLS, treat UnexpectedEof or a read_tls of 0 without close_notify as HttpError::Protocol (truncated), or require Content-Length or chunked for unpinned files; pinning sizes and hashes for vocab.json and merges.txt also closes it.

p0012-security-appimagetool-continuous-u.action: Download a pinned appimagetool release by tag and verify a recorded SHA-256 before chmod +x and execution (also when reusing the cached file).

p0012-security-sign-unpinned-trusted-sig.action: Pin the package version in the URL and verify a recorded SHA-256 (or the package's NuGet signature) before extracting and loading the dlib.

p0012-security-web-serve-windows-absolut.action: Reject rel values containing ':' or any non-Normal path component (use Path::components and require Component::Normal only), and canonicalize the result and require it to start with the canonical serve dir; optionally validate the Host header.

security-cr2-slice-width-overflow.action: Sum the widths with checked_add (as sraw.rs does) and reject any slice width greater than the frame's samples per row before slicing.

security-lossy-dng-jpeg-unbounded-alloc.action: Call decode_headers() first and reject a JPEG whose dimensions exceed the chunk's cw x ch (or MAX_SAMPLES), or set max_width/max_height to the chunk dimensions.

security-open-external-windows-cmd-start.action: Do not route file opening through cmd.exe. Use ShellExecuteW through a maintained opener crate (e.g. the opener/open crate or tauri-plugin-opener), or call `explorer.exe <path>` / `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`, so no shell parsing happens. If cmd must stay, validate the path and pass it with raw_arg using cmd-safe quoting and caret-escaping. Add a regression test with a path that contains `&` and `%`.

security-remote-preauth-slot-exhaustion.action: Apply a short pre-authentication deadline (for example a 5 s read timeout until the first valid token line), and only then switch to the full timeout. Optionally cap connections per peer IP.

security-unbounded-sidecar-reads-bypass-.action: Route read_packet and sidecar_contents through the same bounded reader as import (read_sidecar_packet with MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES) and return an actionable error when the sidecar is larger.

findingMessages.p0004-security-download-pinning-invarian: The downloader's stated security invariant says only a model in lightcraft_faces::known::download can be fetched, with the address a pinned constant that is never typed or passed in. download_spec falls back to entries from the user-editable catalog.json, whose `url` is arbitrary. So the app fetches from addresses that are neither built in nor pinned. Integrity still holds via the catalog's required sha256/size, but the documented trust boundary that reviewers and agents rely on is false.
findingMessages.p0004-security-keyword-export-overwrites: keyword.export writes the keyword list with std::fs::write to any caller-supplied `path` (UI, CLI or MCP agent) and never calls Session::check_write_target. The app's stated invariant (originals.rs:1-5) is that files Ember writes for the user never land on a catalogued photo's original or XMP sidecar. Other writers enforce it (image exports via OriginalGuard, export.contactSheet, merge). `keyword.export {path: "/Photos/IMG_0001.xmp"}`, or the original raw path, silently truncates and replaces that file with a text keyword list. That destroys the photo's sidecar edits and metadata, or the original itself.
findingMessages.p0004-security-placenames-unpinned-base: metadata.downloadPlaceNames accepts an undocumented `base` parameter that may be any https:// host (base_allowed only checks the scheme). The fetched files carry no size or SHA-256 pin (`size: None, sha256: None`). They are then written as the gazetteer into `dataset`, which is also a caller-chosen folder. An agent or script driving the command interface can make the app fetch from an arbitrary host and install unverified place data. Reverse geocoding then writes that data into photo metadata (City/State/Country) across the library. This contrasts with the face-model downloader, which pins address, size and hash.
findingMessages.p0006-security-tls-truncation-accepted-a: For https, a TCP close without TLS close_notify (rustls UnexpectedEof), and a raw read_tls of 0, are both returned as a clean end of stream. Length and Chunked bodies catch this, but a response with neither Content-Length nor chunked encoding uses BodyMode::Close, where the 0 marks the body as Done. A network attacker who injects a FIN/RST can then truncate the body undetected. fetch_file keeps unpinned files (size None, sha256 None) once len > 0, and segment/src/fetch/mod.rs:20-21 downloads vocab.json and merges.txt exactly that way, so a truncated merges.txt is installed as complete and silently degrades the tokenizer.
findingMessages.p0012-security-appimagetool-continuous-u: When appimagetool is not on PATH the release packaging script downloads it from the moving `continuous` GitHub release with no version pin or checksum, executes it, and the AppImage it produces embeds that tool's runtime, which runs on every user's machine. A changed or compromised continuous build alters the shipped AppImage runtime without any change in this repository, and the cached copy in CARGO_TARGET_DIR is reused without re-verification.
findingMessages.p0012-security-sign-unpinned-trusted-sig: Azure Trusted Signing downloads whatever version of Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client nuget.org currently serves as latest, with no version pin, hash or signature check, then loads Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll into signtool while AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET and the other signing credentials are in the environment. A changed or compromised latest package executes arbitrary code with release-signing credentials, and an upstream breaking release silently changes the signing path of a release build.
findingMessages.p0012-security-web-serve-windows-absolut: The `cargo xtask web --serve` static server only rejects `..` components and backslashes. On Windows a request such as `GET /C:/Users/<u>/.ssh/id_rsa` yields rel `C:/Users/...`; Path::join with a path carrying a drive prefix replaces the base, so dir.join(rel) reads any file on disk and returns it with 200. The server binds 127.0.0.1 but performs no Host validation, so any local process, or a remote page via DNS rebinding, can read arbitrary developer files while the dev server runs.
findingMessages.security-cr2-slice-width-overflow: The CR2 slice tag (CR2_SLICE) values s[1] and s[2] are taken from the file unbounded (only >0 checked) and summed with an unchecked iter().sum(). A crafted CR2 with, e.g., slices [1, 2^63, 2^63+1] makes the sum wrap to width=1 in release, which passes the total%width check. Mode::Full then executes data[y*width+x0 .. +sw] with sw=2^63 and panics (debug builds panic at the sum). Opening the file in the app crashes the decode thread, or aborts the web build (panic=abort). The sibling sRAW path uses try_fold/checked_add (cr2/sraw.rs:87).
findingMessages.security-lossy-dng-jpeg-unbounded-alloc: For lossy DNG (compression 34892), decode_chunk bounds n=cw*ch*cpp by MAX_SAMPLES, but lossy_jpeg() hands the chunk to zune-jpeg with max width/height 65536 and never compares the JPEG's own frame header with the chunk dimensions before decode(). A tiny crafted DNG whose tile is a JPEG header declaring 65535x65535 RGB (with a truncated body, accepted because strict mode is off) makes the decoder allocate about 12.9 GB of output per tile. Tiles are decoded in parallel, so this exhausts memory or aborts on allocation failure. The only size check (line 239) runs after the allocation.
findingMessages.security-open-external-windows-cmd-start: On Windows, with no external editor configured, open_external runs `cmd /C start "" <path>` and passes the photo path as an ordinary argument. Rust's Windows argument quoting only wraps arguments that contain a space or tab, and cmd.exe does not follow the MSVC escaping rules, so its metacharacters (&, |, ^, %VAR%) stay live. The path comes from the library: Edit in External Editor (photo.editInExternal -> photo.editExternal result path) sends it through lc_native openExternalEditor. Importing and then editing a photo named like `IMG&calc&.jpg` (no spaces) makes cmd run `calc` as a separate command. Any legitimate filename with an unspaced `&` also fails to open the right file.
findingMessages.security-remote-preauth-slot-exhaustion: The denoise server counts a connection against max_connections (default 8) when it is accepted, before any token check, and each connection may stay idle for the full 120 s read timeout. Any host that can reach the port, without knowing the token, can open 8 connections and send nothing, repeating every 2 minutes. Every legitimate client then gets 'server busy', so the remote GPU is denied to its owner. The listener is meant for a LAN/VPN, which limits who can reach it.
findingMessages.security-unbounded-sidecar-reads-bypass-: Import caps a sidecar at MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES (4 MiB, import.rs:648-662), but read_packet (photo.readMetadataFromFile and other re-reads) reads any found .xmp whole with read_to_string, and for raws reads the entire original into memory; sidecar_contents (every save and XMP auto-write) likewise std::fs::read()s the existing sidecar unbounded. A hostile or corrupt multi-GB IMG_0001.xmp next to a photo makes the allocation fail, which aborts the process: a local file turns a metadata command into a crash, against the repo's own 'cap allocations sized by input' rule.

lensFindings.action: Do not route file opening through cmd.exe. Use ShellExecuteW through a maintained opener crate (e.g. the opener/open crate or tauri-plugin-opener), or call `explorer.exe <path>` / `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler`, so no shell parsing happens. If cmd must stay, validate the path and pass it with raw_arg using cmd-safe quoting and caret-escaping. Add a regression test with a path that contains `&` and `%`.
lensFindings.failureScenario: On Windows, with no external editor configured, open_external runs `cmd /C start "" <path>` and passes the photo path as an ordinary argument. Rust's Windows argument quoting only wraps arguments that contain a space or tab, and cmd.exe does not follow the MSVC escaping rules, so its metacharacters (&, |, ^, %VAR%) stay live. The path comes from the library: Edit in External Editor (photo.editInExternal -> photo.editExternal result path) sends it through lc_native openExternalEditor. Importing and then editing a photo named like `IMG&calc&.jpg` (no spaces) makes cmd run `calc` as a separate command. Any legitimate filename with an unspaced `&` also fails to open the right file.

lensFindings.action: Apply a short pre-authentication deadline (for example a 5 s read timeout until the first valid token line), and only then switch to the full timeout. Optionally cap connections per peer IP.
lensFindings.failureScenario: The denoise server counts a connection against max_connections (default 8) when it is accepted, before any token check, and each connection may stay idle for the full 120 s read timeout. Any host that can reach the port, without knowing the token, can open 8 connections and send nothing, repeating every 2 minutes. Every legitimate client then gets 'server busy', so the remote GPU is denied to its owner. The listener is meant for a LAN/VPN, which limits who can reach it.

lensFindings.failureScenario: keyword.export writes the keyword list with std::fs::write to any caller-supplied `path` (UI, CLI or MCP agent) and never calls Session::check_write_target. The app's stated invariant (originals.rs:1-5) is that files Ember writes for the user never land on a catalogued photo's original or XMP sidecar. Other writers enforce it (image exports via OriginalGuard, export.contactSheet, merge). `keyword.export {path: "/Photos/IMG_0001.xmp"}`, or the original raw path, silently truncates and replaces that file with a text keyword list. That destroys the photo's sidecar edits and metadata, or the original itself.

lensFindings.failureScenario: metadata.downloadPlaceNames accepts an undocumented `base` parameter that may be any https:// host (base_allowed only checks the scheme). The fetched files carry no size or SHA-256 pin (`size: None, sha256: None`). They are then written as the gazetteer into `dataset`, which is also a caller-chosen folder. An agent or script driving the command interface can make the app fetch from an arbitrary host and install unverified place data. Reverse geocoding then writes that data into photo metadata (City/State/Country) across the library. This contrasts with the face-model downloader, which pins address, size and hash.

lensFindings.failureScenario: Import caps a sidecar at MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES (4 MiB, import.rs:648-662), but read_packet (photo.readMetadataFromFile and other re-reads) reads any found .xmp whole with read_to_string, and for raws reads the entire original into memory; sidecar_contents (every save and XMP auto-write) likewise std::fs::read()s the existing sidecar unbounded. A hostile or corrupt multi-GB IMG_0001.xmp next to a photo makes the allocation fail, which aborts the process: a local file turns a metadata command into a crash, against the repo's own 'cap allocations sized by input' rule.

lensFindings.failureScenario: For https, a TCP close without TLS close_notify (rustls UnexpectedEof), and a raw read_tls of 0, are both returned as a clean end of stream. Length and Chunked bodies catch this, but a response with neither Content-Length nor chunked encoding uses BodyMode::Close, where the 0 marks the body as Done. A network attacker who injects a FIN/RST can then truncate the body undetected. fetch_file keeps unpinned files (size None, sha256 None) once len > 0, and segment/src/fetch/mod.rs:20-21 downloads vocab.json and merges.txt exactly that way, so a truncated merges.txt is installed as complete and silently degrades the tokenizer.

lensFindings.action: Sum the widths with checked_add (as sraw.rs does) and reject any slice width greater than the frame's samples per row before slicing.
lensFindings.failureScenario: The CR2 slice tag (CR2_SLICE) values s[1] and s[2] are taken from the file unbounded (only >0 checked) and summed with an unchecked iter().sum(). A crafted CR2 with, e.g., slices [1, 2^63, 2^63+1] makes the sum wrap to width=1 in release, which passes the total%width check. Mode::Full then executes data[y*width+x0 .. +sw] with sw=2^63 and panics (debug builds panic at the sum). Opening the file in the app crashes the decode thread, or aborts the web build (panic=abort). The sibling sRAW path uses try_fold/checked_add (cr2/sraw.rs:87).

lensFindings.action: Call decode_headers() first and reject a JPEG whose dimensions exceed the chunk's cw x ch (or MAX_SAMPLES), or set max_width/max_height to the chunk dimensions.
lensFindings.failureScenario: For lossy DNG (compression 34892), decode_chunk bounds n=cw*ch*cpp by MAX_SAMPLES, but lossy_jpeg() hands the chunk to zune-jpeg with max width/height 65536 and never compares the JPEG's own frame header with the chunk dimensions before decode(). A tiny crafted DNG whose tile is a JPEG header declaring 65535x65535 RGB (with a truncated body, accepted because strict mode is off) makes the decoder allocate about 12.9 GB of output per tile. Tiles are decoded in parallel, so this exhausts memory or aborts on allocation failure. The only size check (line 239) runs after the allocation.

lensFindings.action: Reject rel values containing ':' or any non-Normal path component (use Path::components and require Component::Normal only), and canonicalize the result and require it to start with the canonical serve dir; optionally validate the Host header.
lensFindings.failureScenario: The `cargo xtask web --serve` static server only rejects `..` components and backslashes. On Windows a request such as `GET /C:/Users/<u>/.ssh/id_rsa` yields rel `C:/Users/...`; Path::join with a path carrying a drive prefix replaces the base, so dir.join(rel) reads any file on disk and returns it with 200. The server binds 127.0.0.1 but performs no Host validation, so any local process, or a remote page via DNS rebinding, can read arbitrary developer files while the dev server runs.

lensFindings.action: Pin the package version in the URL and verify a recorded SHA-256 (or the package's NuGet signature) before extracting and loading the dlib.
lensFindings.failureScenario: Azure Trusted Signing downloads whatever version of Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client nuget.org currently serves as latest, with no version pin, hash or signature check, then loads Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll into signtool while AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET and the other signing credentials are in the environment. A changed or compromised latest package executes arbitrary code with release-signing credentials, and an upstream breaking release silently changes the signing path of a release build.

lensFindings.action: Download a pinned appimagetool release by tag and verify a recorded SHA-256 before chmod +x and execution (also when reusing the cached file).
lensFindings.failureScenario: When appimagetool is not on PATH the release packaging script downloads it from the moving `continuous` GitHub release with no version pin or checksum, executes it, and the AppImage it produces embeds that tool's runtime, which runs on every user's machine. A changed or compromised continuous build alters the shipped AppImage runtime without any change in this repository, and the cached copy in CARGO_TARGET_DIR is reused without re-verification.
